articles.title: From League of Legends to K-pop Sensations: The K/DA Story
articles.summary: The inside story of how League of Legends developer Riot Games created K/DA, a K-pop group that topped the charts.
articles.body:
Riot's beloved music group is back. K/DA has reemerged after six years of silence with a brand new single , Firestarter, and an EP will soon follow. Now is as good a time as any to revisit our deep-dive on how a group of League of Legends characters became K-pop sensations, featuring interviews with Madison Beer, Jaira Burns, and Riot staff.

K/DA is a virtual music group; a quartet of animated digital stars that sing infectious, K-pop inspired songs. At first glance, it doesn't look all that different to a band like Gorillaz. But the all-girl act’s catchy bops and slick music videos disguise an unusual origin: K/DA is a group of characters from League of Legends, and its music was made by a video game developer.

This is the inside story of how the studio behind League of Legends took on the music industry and created a pop sensation.

K/DA has amassed over 600 million views on its official YouTube videos. The group has almost three million monthly listeners on Spotify, has won six awards, and has topped the World Digital Song charts three times. With a certified gold record, a trio of hit singles, and a popular EP to its name, K/DA has been a huge success for Riot Games.

The story of that success starts over a decade ago. Back then, League of Legends was quickly growing into one of the most popular video games in the world. As such, it’s unsurprising that the studio was looking to explore other potential opportunities for the universe and its huge roster of characters. Some of those opportunities led to comics and an upcoming Netflix TV series. But the most unusual direction Riot took was music.

“Most of us are fans of, and passionate about, music,” says Toa Dunn, head of Riot Games Music. “It's our way to really invest and express ourselves. We take music to not just be a complimentary thing, but we like to lead with it.”

The developer’s earliest moves into the music scene came through finding songs for the League of Legends World Championship tournaments (better known as ‘Worlds’). Each year, Riot collaborates with bands and artists for the competition’s huge opening show. Among the most famous is Imagine Dragons, who debuted the song ‘Warriors’ at Worlds 2014.

But Riot had larger ambitions than just an annual anthem. It wanted to create a “music universe”, where alternate versions of League of Legends characters would become musicians. The seeds for that universe were planted in 2010 with Pentakill, a set of heavy metal-inspired skins for a handful of League of Legends characters. But Riot soon saw an opportunity to go beyond cosmetics.

“Seeing fans gravitate towards Pentakill as a band, we just asked ourselves ‘Well, what if they were a band?’” says Dunn.

And so in 2014 Pentakill was made for real. Aiming to be more than just a marketing tie-in, Riot collaborated with big names from the world of metal to ensure authenticity. Former Masterplan frontman Jørn Lande provided vocals, and was joined by DragonForce’s original singer, ZP Theart. With former Nine Inch Nails member Danny Lohner on production, Riot created an eight-track metal album called Smite & Ignite.

The album exploded. It hit the Billboard Top 40 and took the No. 1 spot on iTunes’ Metal and Rock charts. It was immediately clear that Riot was onto something good. And so in 2017 Riot recorded a second album, Grasp of the Undying, this time working with Motley Crue’s Tommy Lee. And once again, Pentakill hit the top spot on iTunes’ Metal charts.

But Riot had no intention of stopping at two chart-toppers. And so the music team began to look for a new challenge...

South Korea is one of the most important countries for Riot. It is home to one of the largest League of Legends player bases, as well as the most successful team in the game’s professional scene. Basically, League of Legends and Korea are a perfect match. But Korean pop is also one of the fastest growing music genres on the planet, expanding well beyond its birth nation and into the West. This gradual rise of K-pop in the Western consciousness had worked its way into the personal playlists of staff at Riot Games.

“We were hitting a time in collective pop culture consciousness that K-pop was just about at the tip of everyone's tongue,” says Patrick Morales, Principal Creative Director at Riot Games Music. “By 2018 Psy's Gangnam Style was a thing that was a global phenomenon. BTS, which were previously only in Korea, had started to pierce through the veil of mainstream pop culture consciousness.

“It was around that time that we thought, ‘You know what? I think we do have something really cool to say here, something that we can add to the conversation in pop music',” he adds.

With K-pop on everyone’s minds, the Riot Games Music team set to work on finding the sound they wanted to work with for their next project. And so began the process of creating the next League of Legends virtual band; an all-girl pop group called K/DA.

“When we first started, we were trying to figure out what was a K/DA sound,” Morales recalls. “When we sat down with our composer, Sebastian [Najand], I think the thing that we were all really attracted to was the idea that if we had to really describe a pop sound that we were going for, it would come down to two words: hard-hitting and fun.”

Najand, who was finding inspiration in acts such as 4Minute and Skrillex at the time, had his own idea for what would become K/DA’s debut track. “This kind of non-stop propulsion throughout the entire song is something we wanted,” he says. “Something really intense, really driving, nothing downtempo.”

But the song was just one part of the project. The band needed members. Like with Pentakill, the journey to finding K/DA’s four singers began with a cosmetic. Riot had created a popstar skin for the character Ahri a few years previously. Inspired by this, Riot positioned Ahri as the leader of the group, and built the rest of the lineup around her.

“A lot of these characters are really inspired by their personalities, their backstories of who they are as champions within League of Legends,” explains Morales. “But we were able to find these really neat parallels to how we could express that into reality as actual credible pop star tropes. And I think that's what helped make the magic of K/DA happen.”

Ahri was joined by Akali, Evelynn, and Kai’sa to complete the all-women group. Within the game world of Runeterra, the four are unlikely allies. However, as a K-pop group, the roster makes sense.

“When you look at K/DA it does really have the K-pop feel,” observes Hye Jin Lee, Ph.D., Clinical Assistant Professor of Communication at University of Southern California. Lee specialises in K-pop, and notes a number of authentic elements in K/DA’s design.

“We see that clearly Ahri is the visual,” Lee notes. “She's the leader because she's the one who formed the group. In K-pop there's always a visual member. And then we see Akali, who is the main rapper, and then Evelynn as the diva, the main vocalist. Then Kai'Sa is the main dancer. They all have a role and responsibility they take as a group. They compliment each other and bring the best results. That's what K-pop is about, combining members to bring the best results, and in that sense I think K/DA is very K-pop like.”

Authenticity was important to Riot. While K/DA could never be a ‘true’ K-pop band due to its development in America, it needed to capture the essence of that music scene. “That was a big thing in my head as the song was being developed, what will K-pop fans think of it?” Najand recalls. “Will it stand up to all the songs that I've liked and things like that?”

It was vital that K/DA’s first single sounded as authentic as possible, because it was the song that would elevate them from a group of video game characters to genuine pop stars.

K/DA’s debut track was Pop/Stars, an infectious and energetic single that weaves between fierce verses, melodic bridges, and an anthemic chorus.

“None of the song writers had experience working in the K-pop industry, but it worked,” says Lee. “And here's why: K-pop includes a lot of different forms of music. There are a lot of different genres that are mashed in. There's hip-hop, R&B, rap, house, EDM. You name it, you'll find it in K-pop. Music wise, anything can be K-pop, it's just how it's delivered.”

“We definitely wanted the fusion,” says Najand. “Because a lot of K-pop bands also have a rapping section, they have a singing section, and all that. So, we definitely wanted to do that. We also wanted to have a multilingual approach, Korean and English in this case.”

With a mix of Korean and English vocals, Riot needed to pull together appropriate artists from the worlds of Western pop and K-pop to bring K/DA to life. A careful search brought together the ideal line-up; the Korean lyrics would be performed by Soyeon and Miyeon, two members of the hit K-pop band (G)I-dle. For English vocals, Riot approached American artists Madison Beer and Jaira Burns.

Riot had previously discussed the potential of a music project with Beer. “We were planning to do something for I would say two years,” she recalls. “And then K/DA came as an idea and it felt really perfect and authentic, and the best call to action. The second that the idea was even brought up, we all were like, ‘Yeah, that's what we should be doing.'"

Burns was the last to join the project. “I remember they had Madison picked out already,” she says. “They had the two (G)I-dle girls picked out already, and then they were looking for the last person. So they hit [record label] Interscope... ‘Do you guys have anybody that you think might work for this?’ And so, [Interscope] pitched my name.”

By this time, Riot’s music team had put together a version of Pop/Stars that was nearly ready to go into the studio with. When presented with the track, Beer was surprised. Her brother was a big fan of League of Legends, and the single was not the song she expected to be made for that game.

“I definitely thought it was going to be a little more soundtrack sounding,” says Beer. “Something that would play in the background when people are playing the game. But then it's this super bad-ass song that's empowering and has this awesome message. It was definitely not what I expected, in the best way.”

With the group assembled, Riot set to work recording the track. Madison Beer and Jaira Burns provided the vocals for Evelynn and Kai’Sa, while Soyeon and Miyeon brought Ahri and Akali to life. Each artist had their own way that they approached this character work; either staying true to their own style, or getting lost in a new personality.

“I pretty much just try to bring as much authentic authenticity of myself as possible,” says Burns. “I was very open with Riot about it. But they really were dope as hell and let me just go off and sing it how I wanted to. So I really just brought my raspy edginess to it and tried to be as Jaira as possible on it.”

Beer had an alternative approach. “I threw myself out the window and I was like, ‘Okay, while we're recording, you're Evelynn. Dial that in’,” she says. “It was something I had never done before, I had never played a character in a song. So it was really fun experimenting with my vocals and getting into this more evil, sexy tone.”

Together, the combination of English and Korean voices created the core of the K/DA sound. It was something that wasn’t exactly pure K-Pop, but it made sense to Riot.

“I think before K/DA, most people wouldn't imagine (G)I-dle next to Madison Beer, next to Jaira Burns,” says Dunn. “You just don't really see that happen much, but it made sense here when you really thought about it. There's this kind of diversity and globalness to it. I think that's what helps elevate it to where people can connect to it, whether you are from the K-pop world or if you are from the pop world.”

Riot had put together what it saw as the perfect group and a killer track for K/DA, but that was just the first steps of the band’s planned debut. Pop/Stars would be accompanied by an animated music video that would help establish the tone of the band. Despite being League of Legends characters, K/DA does not exist in the game’s world of Runeterra, and so it was important that the video anchored them in a credible reality.

“Looking at pop music, artists often tap into this element of fantasy to elevate the aesthetic and storytelling of their art,” Morales explains. “It's what gives musicians this mythic quality. It makes them feel mysterious, special, and timeless. K/DA is unique in the sense that we already come from a place of fantasy. These are characters from a game, these are ninjas, demons, assassins. So where do you go there?

“The answer was actually pretty simple,” he reveals. “You go the other direction, you find ways to root them in reality, you find ways to make them feel believable as an actual pop group. So that was the big opportunity for us, where we could re-contextualize what people would normally expect as characters of a video game, now as musicians in our world. That was the unique direction that we decided to take.”

With this idea in mind, the music video features K/DA’s larger-than-life members singing in humdrum urban environments. Ahri relaxes in a laundromat, while Akali raps on a NYC-style subway train. For League of Legends fans, it would be clear that we’re not in Runeterra anymore.

The artists, the song, and the music video were the first three components of K/DA’s debut. The last piece of the puzzle, though, had to be something special. The first reveal of the group had to be huge. It had to be unforgettable. Luckily, Riot had just the thing.

“We wanted them to perform at Worlds,” Dunn recalls. “The year before, we had landed an AR dragon in the middle of the stadium. And so we're like, ‘Okay, with that technology, could we have a band perform.’”

The live performance would feature the real vocalists performing on a stadium stage in front of a huge audience. For anyone watching on the livestream, though, CGI versions of K/DA would also be performing side-by-side with their human counterparts.

“It's pretty strange performing with someone who's not physically there,” says Beer. “But you know that everyone who's watching at home can see them. And obviously, we were really thoroughly prepared for that. We had their markings on the stage where we knew they were going to spawn up and whatnot.”

The show itself was a huge milestone for the real people behind K/DA. “It was definitely a moment where I felt it just all meshed and became real,” Burns says.

“It was really awesome seeing everyone's faces light up in the crowd,” recalls Beer. “It was an honor and it was really fulfilling.”

Pop/Stars was revealed to the world on November 2, 2018 at the League of Legends World Championships. It immediately went viral, with the music video racking up 100 million views in just one month. The single topped Billboard’s World Digital Song Sales, made it to #5 on the Apple Pop Music charts, and hit #1 on Apple’s K-Pop charts. K/DA was a success.

But that was just the beginning. Riot wanted more.

“The big question we had was, ‘Okay, how are we going to follow up on Pop/Stars?’” says Najand. “‘How are we going to make it as cool and hopefully liked by people, but not the same?’ Because we could do another Pop/Stars, but we didn't want it to just feel like the same song over again. And also, we wanted to do more songs than just one.”

The answer to this question was to create All Out, a five-track EP that featured songs focusing on each member of K/DA.

“We wanted All Out to be ‘They're here’,” Dunn explains. “It wasn't a one time, one viral moment of Pop/Stars. We wanted fans to be able to dive deeper into their personalities. They're K/DA, but there's also members of K/DA.”

“Each member was basically the creative producer/director of each song and the music video,” he adds. “So if you were like, ‘Oh, who is Evelynn?’ Listen to her song, listen to the words. You start to see how she sees the world, and potentially how the world sees her.”

At the centre of this EP would be a brand new anthem. “We knew we wanted the big single that was going to be performed live, that would be the follow-up to Pop/Stars,” says Najand.

That track would be called More, and demonstrate a new approach to K/DA’s sound. “We wanted to do something a little bit more grand sounding,” says Najand. “Pop/Stars is very fast. You're kind of sprinting. We wanted More to be slightly more laid back.”

To further explore the group’s potential, Riot decided to work with a variety of new people alongside the existing K/DA artists. Alternative vocalists were brought in for some tracks, including members of the K-pop group Twice. A new character, Seraphine, was added to the group as a guest vocalist on More, voiced by Chinese singer Lexie Liu. Riot also collaborated with a songwriter who had already made a significant mark in the world of K-pop: Rebecca Johnson. Better known as Bekuh Boom, she has written for Blackpink, one of Korea’s most recognizable pop groups, among others. She co-wrote all five of the tracks on All Out.

“So with Bekuh, what was cool is she has this different attitude to her delivery and rap that we wanted to explore,” Najand explains. “That's kind of the big thing that we wanted, that kind of extra attitude, especially with The Baddest and all the other raps. We wanted that to really be at the forefront of the experience.”

“Although Rebecca Johnson is not a K-pop artist and she's not Korean, because of her participation and work in a lot of K-pop songs I do feel a lot of K-pop influence in All Out,” says Lee. “All the songs that involve (G)I-dle and Twice definitely have a K-pop feel.”

All Out released in 2020. Its two singles - The Baddest and More - both hit number one on the Billboard World Digital Song Sales, and the EP itself hit number one on Billboard’s US Heatseekers Album chart. It has been streamed millions of times on Spotify. Once again, K/DA had found success.

And so that leaves one question. What next?

“With K/DA, a lot of people have been talking about if this is going to be the future of music?” says Lee. “Are we going to see more virtual groups?”

“For me, what we need to watch out for is how a lot of K-pop companies are starting to invest in gaming, and how gaming companies have started to invest in K-pop,” Lee adds, pointing to MMO publisher NCSoft’s creation of Universe, a “K-pop platform” where the fandom can unite and watch virtual concerts.

As for Riot, K/DA has opened the door to a whole new audience. “After we saw the success of [K/DA], we decided to run some life studies,” says Morales. “Who was really watching this, where were all these views coming from, where's the conversation starting, as far as how these characters have really accumulated traction in mainstream consciousness?

“What we found was that out of all the people that interacted with K/DA in some fashion, whether that was making fan art, watching the video, talking about it on social media, a good half of them had never even played League of Legends,” he reveals.

Riot continues to see value in its virtual bands and the reach they have beyond League of Legends. Since starting K/DA, the studio has set up a third band: True Damage, a hip-hop group featuring Becky G. And so the developer’s musical universe continues to grow and evolve.

“Our team is really starting to focus on what is the future of our music universe,” says Dunn. “Whether it's Pentakill, whether it's True Damage, K/DA, DJ Sona. We have a lot of these compelling bands or artists in these different genres. There's that storytelling element to it, too. Do they collide? Do they come together like you saw with Seraphine and K/DA? It becomes a really interesting platform to tell a story.”

“I guess offering something new every time is what we were trying to do,” says Najand. “A lot of K-pop bands have their evolution over time, their sound kind of grows, and so we probably want something similar where someone can look back at K/DA's older songs and see a path, and a story within all that.”

Virtual groups may have put Riot on the musical map, but that’s not the only aspect of the industry that the developer wants to innovate in. Riot’s latest creation is Sessions; a collection of copyright-free music that creatives such as streamers and YouTubers can use for no cost.

“It can be hard to be a content creator at times,” recognises Dunn. “And so, we want to help make that easier by providing what we believe to be quality music. Music that we think they're going to love to listen to, but not have to worry about certain things.”

And beyond Sessions… well, not even Riot knows yet. At least, it won’t say just yet. But the team does know that music will continue to be important. That could potentially mean growing beyond League of Legends and working with the characters of Valorant, Riot’s first-person shooter.

“We're going to continue to look at opportunities for music around Valorant,” says Dunn. “I think music is just core to us here at Riot. I'd be surprised if we did anything and music wasn't really thought of as a part of that experience. We're going to continue to do that with pretty much everything, I would assume.”

From a heavy metal-inspired character skin to a collection of license-free music designed for content creators, Riot’s music story has followed a surprising and varied path. K/DA is the slick and glitzy star of this tale, and it demonstrates that the company sees music as more than just a marketing gimmick. Through the group’s success, Riot has found a new creative playground in which to experiment and evolve. If this lightning can be re-bottled remains to be seen, but one thing is clear: Riot isn’t just a video games developer now. It’s something more.

Matt Purslow is IGN's UK News and Entertainment Writer. Simon Cardy is IGN's UK Video Producer. Additional reporting by Mike Mamon, IGN's Syndication and Digital Strategist.

articles.title: Widdecombe suspect had 'particular hostility to Reform', court told
articles.summary: Kerry is charged with the murder of the 78-year-old former Conservative minister and Reform UK spokeswoman.
articles.body:
The man accused of murdering Ann Widdecombe had a "particular hostility to Reform", prosecutors alleged on Friday.

They said Joshua Kerry, 28, "had an extreme left wing and/or anti-establishment mindset".

The prosecution also told the Old Bailey Widdecombe's murder had a "terrorist connection" as it was "politically and ideologically motivated".

Last week, Kerry, who had already been charged with Widdecombe's murder in July, was charged with a second offence of preparing terrorist acts.

He is accused of "online reconnaissance" of prominent people and institutions, travelling to Nigel Farage's home in South London on 19 April 2025, and trying to break into it 15 months before Widdecombe was killed.

Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb agreed to the prosecution request to join the two charges into one case.

The prosecution argued they were "inextricably linked".

Kerry appeared in court by video link from Belmarsh prison wearing a prison-issue grey sweatshirt.

The judge set a date for a five-week trial on 8 June next year.

Nicholas Lumley KC, defending, told the court that Kerry was likely to contest all the charges against him.

Kerry was charged in July with the murder of 78-year-old Widdecombe, a former Conservative minister and Reform spokeswoman.

Widdecombe was found dead on 9 July at her home in Haytor, Devon, having sustained serious injuries.

The former Tory MP was hit on the head with a hammer 21 times at her home as she ate lunch, prosecutors said during a hearing at Westminster Magistrates' Court in July.

She served as Conservative MP for Maidstone and the Weald in Kent for 23 years and was appointed to ministerial roles in Sir John Major's government in the 1990s.

Following her departure from the Commons, Widdecombe appeared on the BBC's Strictly Come Dancing in 2010 and was a runner-up on Celebrity Big Brother eight years later.

articles.title: Yemen fighting expands as Houthis attack Saudi airport: What to know
articles.summary: Saudi coalition blames Houthi group for the missile attack on the main international airport in Riyadh.
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia has said it will “firmly” retaliate against an attack on Riyadh’s international airport, in which at least 12 people were killed, with United States President Donald Trump calling the attack “terrible”.

The Saudi-led military coalition on Sunday blamed Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi group for Saturday’s attack on King Khalid international airport, describing it as a “full-fledged war crime”. The Houthis have not claimed responsibility for the latest strike.

However, on Sunday, the Houthis, also known as Ansar Allah (Supporters of God), renewed ⁠⁠⁠⁠their warning to ⁠⁠⁠⁠airlines, airport workers, and travellers against using ‌‌‌‌Saudi airports, saying the warning should be taken seriously ⁠⁠⁠⁠and that the ⁠⁠⁠⁠kingdom “bore responsibility for failed interceptions”.

The attack comes amid escalating fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces following the collapse of a United Nations-brokered ceasefire largely in place since 2022.

The fighting has raised fears of a wider regional confrontation, with Trump suggesting the US could join Saudi military operations against the Houthis.

Dania Thafer, executive director at the Gulf International Forum, said Saudi Arabia will likely hit back at the Houthis “pretty hard”.

“I still think that the Saudis probably want de-escalation. They don’t want long-term escalation, but the Houthis are making it very difficult by not only being a threat to Saudi national security but also a threat to international maritime security,” Thafer said. “So this battle is much bigger than just a tit-for-tat.”

According to Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA), a missile struck King Khalid airport in Riyadh on Saturday. It killed 12 people and wounded 309 others, some of them critically.

The dead included four Saudi nationals, two Bangladeshis and one citizen each from the US, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan. It was the deadliest attack on the kingdom in more than a decade.

“The cowardly terrorist attack by the Terrorist Houthi Militia … which resulted in deaths and injuries among civilian passengers and airport staff, constitutes a full-fledged war crime,” coalition spokesman Major-General Turki al-Malki said in a statement on X.

The Houthis, who have yet to take responsibility for the attack, said on Sunday they “renew their warning to all aviation companies, experts, employees, workers, and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, because they are exposed to targeting and are a theatre of operations by our forces”.

“They urge everyone to take our warnings seriously, and Saudi Arabia bears responsibility for any failed interceptions,” military spokesperson Yahya Saree said in a post on X.

Airport operations were suspended, with flights cancelled or diverted. Schools across Riyadh were ordered to switch to remote learning for a week following the attack.

The attacks have disrupted international flights, with several airlines suspending services to Saudi destinations. Later on Saturday, the Saudi-led coalition said a projectile had fallen near King Fahd international airport in Dammam in the country’s east.

Al Jazeera’s Yousef Mawry, reporting from the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa, said the Iran-backed group was retaliating by attacking what it called Saudi Arabia’s “most precious assets”, which are Aramco oil facilities and the airport in Riyadh.

“Although Saudi Arabia has said it will retaliate, let’s not forget that it’s carried out many air strikes across Yemen, and the Yemeni group is still able to launch ballistic missiles and drones towards Saudi Arabia,” he added.

What other areas have the Houthis targeted?

The Iran-aligned Houthis have launched a series of missile and drone attacks targeting airports, military installations and oil facilities across Saudi Arabia, including areas near the border with Yemen.

On Monday, attacks on King Abdullah bin Abdulaziz airport in the southwestern city of Jizan and Najran international airport wounded three people and caused material damage, according to the GACA.

On Tuesday, attacks on Abha airport and Riyadh airport killed three people and wounded 36 others, according to Saudi authorities.

The Houthis also claimed to have targeted an Aramco oil refinery in Rabigh, on Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea coast, with missiles and drones, saying the attack caused a fire. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the claim.

The Houthis imposed a maritime embargo on Saudi Arabia in July following the outbreak of the latest round of fighting.

Yasmeen al-Eryani, the executive director for knowledge production at Sanaa Center, said the Houthis are trying to put “maximum pressure” on Saudi Arabia.

“But they’re also mobilising the internal front lines in a really major way, moving even away from the west coast battle into Taiz and more densely populated areas,” al-Eryani, from the think tank based in government-controlled Aden, told Al Jazeera.

“We could see further mobilisation; they have very high momentum. They will probably continue to capitalise on that momentum, internally,” she said, adding that “the [Houthi] cross-border attacks” will put pressure across the region.

Al-Eryani added that the Houthis were “provoking” Saudi Arabia, the US and regional states, which could potentially join in the conflict.

The Houthi-affiliated media on Sunday reported an air attack on Naqil al-Zarbi in the Hayfan district of Yemen’s Taiz governorate in southwestern Yemen, as well as a missile attack on the Sahar district in the northern province of Saada.

Forces belonging to Yemen’s internationally recognised government also released footage purportedly showing the downing of a Houthi drone over Mount Sabr in Taiz.

Meanwhile, Saudi-led coalition spokesman Major-General Turki al-Maliki said early on Sunday that forces intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis towards al-Kharj province, as well as a drone in the kingdom’s Eastern province.

On Saturday, Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili, the spokesman for Yemeni government forces, said at least 1,150 Houthis were killed in almost 2,000 targeted operations across the country since the internationally recognised government’s counteroffensive began.

He said the army had destroyed Houthi ammunition dumps and at least 180 combat, transport and supply vehicles operated by the Houthis, adding that ground forces “continued to advance their assault”.

Al Jazeera was not able to independently verify the competing claims.

Fighting has intensified across several fronts in Yemen, with Saudi-backed government forces launching the Dawn of Yemen offensive on October 4 to recapture Houthi-held territory, including the port city of Mocha and the island of Mayyun.

While the internationally recognised government’s forces said they had retaken Mocha and the Dhubab district near the strait, the Houthis have disputed the claims.

The Houthis have also tightened their siege of Taiz after capturing territory south of the city earlier this month, including al-Turbah. Taiz has been one of the most heavily contested cities in the war.

Fighting has also spread to Marib and al-Jawf, two governorates east of Sanaa, where government forces have reported advances against Houthi positions.

What has been the international response to the Houthi attack on the airport?

The attack has drawn condemnation from the US and the UN, while several foreign governments have warned their citizens to avoid the airport.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed that an American was among those killed and condemned the attacks.

“These reprehensible attacks demonstrate a blatant disregard for innocent civilian life. They must stop now,” Rubio said.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the strike, stressing that attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure violate international law.

The US, Canada, Germany and several other countries issued travel warnings, while some diplomatic missions restricted staff movements through the airport.

Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif described the attack as “heinous” and reaffirmed Islamabad’s commitment to Saudi security.

On October 5, Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia agreed to activate “deterrence measures” under a mutual defence pact and rapidly deploy forces to the Gulf kingdom to counter attacks by Yemen’s Houthis. This came weeks after the three countries signed the Mecca Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement.

Will the US join Saudi strikes against Yemen’s Houthis?

Trump has left open the possibility of US military involvement but has not announced a decision.

“We may. We’re going to look at it,” Trump told reporters on Saturday.

The US president said he planned to speak with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, describing the attack as “not acceptable”.

According to US media reports, Washington has already provided intelligence sharing, target identification and planning assistance for the latest Saudi-backed offensive.

When the Saudi-led coalition intervened in the civil war in March 2015, Washington provided intelligence, logistical assistance and weapons to support its campaign against the Houthis, but did not directly participate in the coalition’s air strikes.

But in 2021, the Biden administration ended support for the Saudi-led offensive in Yemen, citing the humanitarian crisis. More than 100,000 Yemenis were killed and millions were displaced at the time.

articles.title: US Homeland Security defends Nidal Hasan livestream execution bid
articles.summary: Markwayne Mullin rejects concerns that livestreaming the execution of convicted killer Nidal Hasan could fuel radicalisation or make him a martyr.
articles.body:
The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) chief has defended a plan to livestream the execution of convicted killer Nidal Hasan, rejecting claims that it could fuel radicalisation or make him a martyr.

"I don't see an elevated risk," Markwayne Mullin said on Sunday. "I think people need to understand that if you attack America, we will come after you, and we will make sure that the punishment fits the crime."

Hasan, a former US Army Major, is due to be executed by firing squad in December for shooting dead 13 soldiers at the Fort Hood military base in Texas.

The Trump administration has said it plans to livestream his death, prompting shock and concern from both Republicans and Democrats.

President Donald Trump has said he signed off on the execution, but while he approves of the livestream plan, a final decision is yet to be made.

It would be the first public execution in the US in almost a century.

The plan, which was announced by Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth last week , has been heavily criticised by politicians, academics and experts.

Alaskan Republican Senator, Lisa Murkowski, called the decision "gruesome" and said livestreaming an execution was something she would expect "from terrorists and dictators, but not here in America".

"It would give this individual, who deserves no further notoriety, the martyrdom he seeks," she wrote on X , adding that "how we carry out justice matters just as much as the justice itself."

Virginia Democrat Mark Warner said that allowing the public to tune into the execution could heighten the national security risk.

"Beyond the profound moral concerns, a public execution could hand terrorist organizations a propaganda victory, fuel radicalization, and put American service members, diplomats, and citizens overseas at greater risk," he wrote .

But speaking to CBS news programme Face the Nation on Sunday, the DHS secretary rejected these concerns, and insisted the risks had been considered.

"[Hasan] killed 13 individuals on Fort Hood. I have no sympathy for him, and I give absolutely zero thought to the way that this man dies," Mullin told presenter Margaret Brennan.

Who is Nidal Hasan? What to know about US plans to livestream an execution

Public executions in the US stopped nearly a century ago - why are they resuming now?

Nidal Hasan, a former US Army major and psychiatrist from Virginia, admitted to fatally shooting 13 unarmed troops at a crowded medical building at the Fort Hood military base. A further 32 others were injured in the attack.

In court, Hasan apologised for "any mistakes" and said he believed he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan from the US military. Hasan was shot during the attack and now uses a wheelchair.

His execution would be the first by the US military since 1961, and the military's first execution by firing squad since World War Two.

articles.title: Riftbound: Radiance Rarest Cards - Riot Games Music Crossovers Dominate the Set
articles.summary: Riftbound's fifth set, Radiance, features rare showcase cards inspired by Riot Games Music acts: Heartsteel, True Damage, and K/DA. Check out all of the Overnumbered cards in the set along with the rarest card in the entirety of the TCG.
articles.body:
The newest Riftbound set, Radiance, is coming up right around the corner, and with the new set of mechanically exciting cards comes a slew of beautiful collectibles worth the chase, too. Here's a look at some of these cool new cards with commentary about how they came to be from Riftbound executive produce Chengran Chai.

The Riftbound team layers collectibility on top of playability with Alt Art, Overnumbered, and SP cards only when the've completed fine-tuning the mechanics of the set. Some of the rare standouts for Radiance are Riot Games Music crossovers, including the Overnumbered Heartsteel cards, SP K/DA cards, and Overnumbered Ekko, Revolutionary, which features Ekko’s original True Damage skin. The Overnumbered cards also come in the Signature variety, which are the rarest pulls besides the single Ultimate Rare in this set.

“We knew Riot as a whole would have a music moment towards the end of the year, so very early on, we said we would lean into that,” Chai said. However, as a physical game, the Riftbound team needed to finalize many card details before the songs were even composed and the new character designs were finished.

Riftbound: Radiance - Music ONs, SPs, and Alt Runes

“That is why you see… for the K/DA and Heartsteel cards, it is very much their K/DA All Out and Heartsteel 1.0 versions, because the 2.0 versions just weren’t quite ready,” Chai said. “But we thought it would be a great way to showcase Riftbound’s participation… and leverage the broader music moment to allow more fans to see and experience Riftbound as well.”

This original plan didn’t even include teasing Heartsteel’s Riftbound cards in Heartsteel’s new Live My Life music video–the Riot Music Team actually initiated that easter egg, asking the Riftbound team if they wanted the cards in the music video. Of course, they said yes.

Though Riftbound has been very supported from within Riot since the beginning, the somewhat unexpected explosion of its popularity has given Riftbound even more opportunities to be a part of Riot-wide moments. Another example of this is the Riftbound easter egg in Valorant’s Aeris Flex cosmetic.

The Heartsteel Overnumbered cards feature a very unique design, akin to K-pop photo cards, complete with bright motifs, stickers, and Y2K elements. Playing into the photo card inspiration even more, the Heartsteel Overnumbered Signature cards are "signed" by the characters themselves--not the artists like on other Signature cards! Riot Games’ senior Manager of creative development Michelle Mauk spoke about the design process during the Radiance panel at the Riftbound Regional Qualifier (RQ) in Los Angeles , which I highly recommend you watch if you’re interested.

I always feel like renders of Overnumbered cards don’t do them justice, and that’s certainly the case for the Heartsteel cards, too. The texturing and foiling on Riftbound’s most coveted cards are always so impressive to behold in person. I tried to capture the look in the photos of the Overnumbered Ekko, Revolutionary Champion Unit I pulled in the slideshow above, but it's difficult to show all the different patterns, holographics, and gold text in a single picture!

Radiance’s Ultimate Rare ties well into the heavy music theme but is, shockingly, a Battlefield: Packed Amphitheater. This card will be the rarest card in all of Riftbound’s main sets, only appearing in about 0.025% of booster packs, which is approximately 1 in 4,000 packs. That’s a huge rarity uptick from the only other Ultimate Rare, Baron Nasher from Unleashed, with a 0.1% pack rate. The in-person foiling and texturing you can't see in a render does a lot a lot of heavy lifting for this one–and you can get a better look at it, and see some creators’ reactions, in this official PlayRiftbound reel.

Riftbound: Radiance Overnumbered and Alt Art Cards

There are other Overnumbered and Alt Art cards to chase that aren’t musically inclined, too, like the Overnumbererd Mordekaiser Legend IGN exclusively revealed last week . The Overnumbered cards come in a Signature variety as mentioned, which are significantly rarer than the Alt Art cards, but that doesn't take away from how cool some of the Alt Art cards are.

For more on Riftbound's fifth set, Radiance, check out this full hands-on Radiance preview and more from the interview with Chai .

Radiance Pre-Rifts start at local game stores near you on Oct. 16, and I really can’t wait to play some more. With the complexity Radiance introduces, this might not be the best first set to get into, but it’s great for existing players craving more variety and creativity in their deck building. That being said, the Riftbound community has always been nothing but welcoming and helpful at every store I’ve played at, too, so don’t be shy. Otherwise, Radiance booster boxes, packs, and vaults will be available to purchase on Oct. 23.

Casey DeFreitas is the deputy editor of guides at IGN and is playing three more Riftbound Radiance Pre-Rifts this weekend at a local game store, because they're just that much fun. Catch her on socials @ShinyCaseyD .

articles.title: Obras contra enchentes em Franca: veja prazos, custos e situação | G1
articles.standfirst: Com a chegada da temporada de chuvas, intervenções nos córregos Bagres, Cubatão e Palmeiras tentam evitar novos alagamentos. Veja a situação de cada trecho.
articles.summary: Obras contra enchentes em Franca nos córregos Bagres, Cubatão e Palmeiras somam R$ 35,9 milhões. Intervenções buscam conter alagamentos, mas prazos de conclusão vão até 2027.
articles.body:
Obras de combate a enchentes em Franca (SP). — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Franca (SP)

A chegada da primavera traz de volta o alerta para tempestades em Franca (SP), como a de janeiro deste ano, que acumulou mais de 80 milímetros de chuva em apenas duas horas e travou grandes avenidas.

Para evitar novos estragos, a cidade executa três grandes obras de drenagem contratadas por R$ 35,9 milhões com recursos federais e municipais.

Embora as obras estejam dentro do cronograma, as entregas estão previstas apenas para o período entre 2026 e 2027.

Até o momento, segundo dados do Portal da Transparência, foi pago pouco mais de R$ 1 milhão às empresas contratadas. Nas últimas semanas, os trabalhos concentram-se na demolição de antigas travessias, instalação de pranchas metálicas e outras intervenções para estabilização de solo.

Segundo Willian Karan Junior, coordenador executivo do Observatório Social do Brasil (OSB) em Franca, a execução de intervenções durante a estação chuvosa exige atenção para evitar que as próprias obras criem novos obstáculos ao escoamento.

"Alguns trechos já executados podem produzir benefícios localizados, especialmente onde houve ampliação da seção do canal ou melhoria das estruturas de drenagem. Entretanto, enquanto o conjunto não estiver concluído e integrado, não é possível afirmar que as obras oferecerão toda a capacidade de proteção prevista no projeto", afirma.

Ele ressalta que desvios provisórios, escavações e materiais depositados demandam monitoramento constante. "Uma obra incompleta não deve ser considerada, por si só, uma proteção integral contra enchentes", acrescenta.

Abaixo, confira o raio-x de cada frente de trabalho:

🔎A obra no Córrego dos Bagres consiste no alargamento do canal ao longo da Avenida Doutor Antônio Barbosa Filho , no trecho entre a Rua Simão Caleiro e a Avenida Doutor Ismael Alonso y Alonso, além da demolição de uma antiga ponte e da construção de uma nova travessia no encontro com o Córrego Cubatão para eliminar o represamento da água.

💲A intervenção foi orçada na licitação em R$ 24.789.222,77 e contratada em 10 de fevereiro de 2026 junto à Tessalia Construtora e Incorporadora por R$ 22.750.000,00 , com término previsto para 19 de agosto de 2027 . Até o momento, foram pagos R$ 299.940,31 à construtora, o que representa 1,31% do valor do contrato .

✅ O que os operários terminaram de fazer:

furos para os pilares : terminaram de furar o chão para instalar os tubulões, que são grandes estacas fincadas na terra para dar sustentação;

formas de concreto : montaram as molduras das vigas de encabeçamento, que são blocos de concreto que unem essas estacas no topo;

muro de metal : começaram a fincar grandes placas de metal no chão do lado direito, em direção ao shopping, para segurar a terra do barranco;

demolição : a quebra do concreto antigo das paredes do rio entrou na reta final.

🚧 O que estão fazendo e o que vem a seguir:

interdições no trânsito : há máquinas e operários trabalhando nos dois lados da avenida, por isso a pista está funcionando pela metade;

represa temporária : as equipes vão montar uma parede provisória dentro do rio chamada "ensecadeira", que serve para desviar a água, deixando o chão seco para os operários trabalharem com segurança;

montagem do fundo : as equipes vão raspar e nivelar o fundo do córrego para começar a encaixar grandes peças de concreto pré-moldadas.

O coordenador do Observatório Social pondera que o baixo percentual pago não indica atraso nas obras.

"O percentual pago não deve ser automaticamente tratado como percentual físico da obra, pois o pagamento ocorre após medição e liquidação financeira", afirma Willian Karan.

Ele destaca que vistorias de campo identificaram barras de aço compatíveis com o projeto, mas ressalta que a entidade aguarda documentos solicitados via e-SIC, como o cronograma físico-financeiro e relatórios de medição, para confirmar a evolução exata dos trabalhos.

Alagamentos em avenidas são um problema histórico em Franca — Foto: Igor do Vale

🔎A intervenção no Córrego Cubatão prevê o aprofundamento e o alargamento do leito sob o viaduto das avenidas Major Nicácio e Doutor Ismael Alonso y Alonso , nas proximidades do Viaduto Dona Quita e do campus da Uni-Facef. O objetivo é ampliar a vazão de água sob a estrutura viária .

💲Orçada em R$ 10.968.259,63, a obra foi contratada em 4 de maio de 2026 com a empresa Planex Engenharia por R$ 10.264.900,00 , com término em maio de 2027. Segundo extratos públicos consultados, nenhum valor foi pago.

escavação : equipes escavaram e deixaram o canal mais fundo e mais largo;

proteção : equipes colocaram tapumes de madeira ao redor da obra para proteger quem passa por perto.

injeção de cimento : as equipes estão aplicando a técnica de jet grouting, que injeta cimento sob altíssima pressão na terra mole. Isso faz o solo virar um bloco firme ao lado do prédio do Uni-Facef, na direção do SESC e da Avenida Major Nicácio;

interdições no trânsito : algumas faixas estão bloqueadas por causa dos trabalhos, por isso motoristas e pedestres precisam ter atenção à sinalização.

Sobre a ausência de pagamentos registrados para esta frente no Portal da Transparência, o especialista do OSB esclarece que o saldo zerado reflete trâmites burocráticos e não uma paralisação.

"A ausência momentânea de pagamento registrado não significa ausência de execução, pois pode haver serviços realizados em processo de conferência", explica Karan.

🔎A obra no Jardim Palmeiras engloba drenagem, aprofundamento e alargamento do canal afluente do Córrego Engenho Queimado , para conter a erosão das margens e proteger moradias nas proximidades.

💲Com orçamento licitado de R$ 3.332.270,60, o projeto foi contratado por R$ 2.900.000,00 em 19 de fevereiro de 2026 junto ao Consórcio Excoima Infraestrutura e Pavimentações, com término previsto para 31 de outubro de 2026 . Do total contratado, foram pagos R$ 753.911,27 , o que representa 25,99% de execução financeira.

✅ O que os operários terminaram de fazer :

limpeza de pedras : as equipes limparam todos os gabiões, que são gaiolas de arame cheias de pedras empilhadas que seguram a terra;

caixa de água : finalizaram a caixa de passagem de concreto perto do dissipador, que ajuda a controlar a força e a direção da água.

🚧 O que estão fazendo e o que vem a seguir :

nova travessia : a próxima etapa será construir uma nova travessia na Rua Anésio Basílio dos Santos para permitir que carros e pedestres cruzem o canal com segurança.

Com a etapa financeira mais adiantada entre os três lotes, a obra no Palmeiras apresenta avanço visível, mas exige cautela na avaliação final.

"O estágio visível e os registros indicam avanço relevante no Jardim Palmeiras, mas o percentual financeiro não deve ser automaticamente convertido em percentual físico, já que etapas diferentes têm pesos financeiros distintos e todo o sistema precisa estar integrado", avalia o coordenador do OSB.

articles.body:
Official K/DA accounts have been updated for the first time in six years. New profile and banner images continue to show the existing promotional art from the All Out era, now with the addition of hot pink flames. The reactivated accounts have also wiped existing posts, fueling rumors that the virtual girl group is gearing up for a comeback.

K/DA, which debuted at the 2018 League of Legends World Championship, consists of four League champions (Ahri, Akali, Evelynn, and Kai'Sa) voiced by international pop-stars. The group’s first single, aptly called POP/STARS, was the first K-pop song by a girl group to receive RIAA Platinum certification in 2022. The early success of the girl group prompted the release of a full EP, All Out, in 2020.

Since then, the group has pretty much gone dark. K/DA skins still exist in-game, but there’s been no word on new music or performances. Until now.

I’m not asking for much. I just want to see a teaser from K/DA that’s as peak as this. — RainySeason (@CookieNevie) October 13, 2026

I’m not asking for much. I just want to see a teaser from K/DA that’s as peak as this.

An updated banner image continues to use promotional images from the All Out era, showing the main K/DA quartet alongside the era’s guest artist, Seraphine, who was a newly released champion at the time. As of October 13, however, those images also show the addition of hot pink and magenta flames .

Data-mined leaks from earlier this year already raised hopes that the group would have some role in the current season of League of Legends. Details in a Wild Rift update, first spotted by SkinSpotlights , pointed to a potential “Firestarter” skin concept, as well as a new song registered on the ASCAP Repertory.

Other users have interpreted the purple smoke as a sign that K/DA is being added to Fortnite, which is currently using similarly colored imagery for its Fortnitemares event .

The question of K/DA’s return extends beyond Riot, as it also depends on the availability of the four singers associated with the group: Madison Beer, Soyeon, Miyeon, and Jaira Burns.

Online fan accounts recently started circulating the rumor that Beer would be leaving the group. The singer herself was asked about her return to K/DA during her recent Locket tour, saying : "I would love to. It’s not really up to me, although I wish it was. There actually was a conversation a few years ago about doing something again, but I don’t know what happened to it.”

Riot has yet to confirm any rumors about a K/DA comeback, let alone who the group currently includes. The League of Legends World Championship tournament is currently being hosted across the United States, with the Grand Final scheduled for November 14. Given that K/DA made its debut at the Worlds tournament, there’s a possibility we'll hear more over the course of this year's event.

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi missile launched towards Riyadh
articles.summary: Saudi civil defence authority says danger passed after it issued alerts via its national early warning platform.
articles.body:
The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launched towards Saudi Arabia’s capital, Riyadh, as the Yemeni armed group said it carried out more attacks on the kingdom.

Coalition spokesman Major-General Turki al-Maliki on Wednesday announced the thwarted attack on X, days after two separate strikes hit Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport, killing 14 people and injuring hundreds.

The General Directorate of Saudi Civil Defence also issued two alerts through its national early warning platform, later saying the danger had passed. One alert was for the Al-Kharj governorate in Riyadh province, and the other for the capital.

The Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for supporters of God), issued a statement saying they targeted facilities of Saudi ⁠⁠Arabia’s national oil company Aramco in Dhahran, an Aramco refinery in Riyadh, and the capital’s King Khalid international ‌‌airport.

Overnight, the Saudi Ministry of Energy confirmed that the administrative building belonging to Aramco in Dhahran was hit.

Al Jazeera’s Zein Basravi, reporting from the Qatari capital Doha, said any notion that the Saudi-led coalition could contain the conflict to Yemen had been shattered over the last 10 days, which saw the targeting of several sites in Saudi Arabia.

Houthi attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport over the weekend killed 14 people and wounded more than 300 others. Houthi attacks have also been reported on other airports , including the Abha international airport, where two people were killed, and on Aramco facilities.

Meanwhile, Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces have launched a counteroffensive in Yemen to retake coastal territory from the Houthis near the Bab al-Mandeb strait at the entrance to the Red Sea, a vital maritime trade chokepoint.

Fighting in Yemen between the Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces escalated sharply last month, shattering a United Nations-brokered ceasefire that had largely held since 2022.

The Houthis have controlled Yemen’s most populous areas, including the capital Sanaa, since seizing the city in 2014, forcing the internationally recognised government to flee to southern Yemen.

The Muslim World League on Wednesday condemned the continued Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, saying they deliberately target civilians and civilian sites. The league’s secretary-general, Sheikh Mohammad bin Abdulkarim Al-Issa, said their nature confirms “the criminal approach of this terrorist militia in deliberately targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure”.

Meanwhile, Yemen’s Houthi-affiliated Al-Masirah television reported that four air strikes hit the Harib district in the country’s Marib governorate. The results of the attacks were not immediately clear.

Nawaf Obaid, a security and intelligence analyst and senior research fellow at King’s College London, told Al Jazeera that while air strikes are intensifying, the “actual ground war hasn’t really begun” for the Saudi-led coalition.

Obaid broke down the phases in which such an operation could unfold, saying the first phase would be “to hit at basically the power and the energy source that’s allowing the Houthis to operate … tanks, armoured vehicles, trucks”.

Phase two would be to look at the “systematic increase of Houthi control in the region, which is critical,” he said.

Phase three would involve a discussion on how “to start taking back these territories that the Houthis have gained since the beginning of the war”.

Obaid said these “multipronged phases” would include “extra-specialised” troops, especially in mountain warfare, because the Houthis are taking the battlefield into difficult terrain.

articles.title: Milwaukee Brewers: Andrew Vaughn takes playful jab at rookie Cooper Pratt ahead of NLCS Game 3
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers, as of this writing, are about an hour away from first pitch of Game Three of the National League Championship Series. After winning th...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers , as of this writing, are about an hour away from first pitch of Game Three of the National League Championship Series. After winning the first two games at home, Milwaukee will try to finish off the Los Angeles Dodgers on the road. They have already won more games in this year's NLCS than they did last postseason when they were swept by these same Dodgers.

This year's Brewers club, obviously, is much-improved from a year ago. Not only have they received massive contributions from their veterans, but they also have several rookies who have contributed to their success for much of the season.

One of these is shortstop Cooper Pratt , who has impressed his teammates ever since he arrived in the Majors.

Milwaukee Brewers first baseman Andrew Vaughn pokes fun at Cooper Pratt

Prior to Game Three, several Brewers players spoke with the media. Pratt was paired with first baseman Andrew Vaughn, who was asked how much his rookie teammate has matured throughout the course of the season.

"A lot," Vaughn said . "It took a while for him to put his sippy cup down." Pratt recently went viral for drinking Fanta during Milwaukee's celebration following their victory in the NLDS. A devout Mormon, the Brewers shortstop does not drink alcohol.

Vaughn went on to say how impressed he was with Pratt's improvement at the plate and willingness to keep working on getting better.

Indeed, Pratt has been a pleasant surprise at the plate. In the minors, he slashed .257/.354/.380. This, of course, is not terrible, but there were some concerns whether or not he would be able to hit Major League pitching.

After the regular season started, Pratt signed an eight-year contract with Milwaukee despite having yet to make his MLB debut. In 59 minor league games this year, he hit .243/.349/.387.

Since arriving in the Majors, though, he has been one of the Brewers most consistent hitters. In 74 games, he hit .281/.350/.368 with three home runs, 34 RBI, and 19 stolen bases.

Having played in each postseason game Milwaukee has played so far in 2026, the rookie shortstop is hitting .286/.286/.333.

articles.title: Retired US generals call on Pentagon to cancel livestream execution
articles.summary: Livestreaming the execution of Nidal Hasan "will taint the honor of the military that employs it, and a nation that allows it," 72 former officers said in a letter.
articles.body:
A group of 72 retired US generals, admirals, and other high-ranking military officers are pressing the US government to cancel plans to livestream an execution by firing squad.

"We ask the President, our Congressional representatives, and our fellow citizens to act to prevent this barbaric abuse of authority," they wrote in a letter where they also argued the livestream would turn the mass killer into a "martyr".

Last week, the Pentagon announced it would publicly show the 3 December execution of Nidal Hasan, an Army psychiatrist who shot dead 13 unarmed US soldiers at the Fort Hood military base.

Lawmakers from both parties, as well as religious leaders, have criticised the plan.

Last week President Donald Trump said he "absolutely" approved of the livestream plan, but some administration officials are now leaning against it, according to CBS News, the BBC's US media partner. CBS reported thatTrump had not yet made a final decision on the livestream as of Tuesday.

In the open letter released on Wednesday, the former military leaders - which included 45 generals, 12 admirals and several former judge advocates general - said they did not oppose the death penalty being carried out.

But they argued a public execution would violate the US Constitution's protections against cruel and unusual punishment and turn what should be a "solemn and grave punishment" into "a carnival for the enjoyment of voyeurs and spectators".

"This type of exploitative broadcasting - that debases human dignity- will taint the honor of the military that employs it, and a nation that allows it," they also wrote.

"It will be used by our nation's enemies to stoke hatred, harm American soldiers and citizens in the future, and will ensure that Hasan becomes a martyr for attacking and killing his fellow soldiers."

The letter's signatories came from throughout the military and included a handful of officers who retired during Trump's first term. Some also had served during the Iraq and Afghanistan wars.

Hasan said in court that he carried out the shooting at Fort Hood, the deadliest ever non-combat attack on an American base, believing he was protecting Muslims and the Taliban in Afghanistan from the US military. Hasan was shot during the attack and now uses a wheelchair.

Retired Maj Gen Tony Taguba, who led the Army's investigation into reported prisoner abuses at Abu Ghraib in Iraq, and retired Air Force Coll Moe Davis, a prosecutor at the Guatanamo Bay detention centre who called waterboarding torture, signed the letter.

So did Charles Bolden, a US Marine Corps Major General who became the head of Nasa, and a retired Lt Gen Claudia Kennedy, the first woman to become a three-star general in the Army.

Trump has said he signed off on the execution, but while he approves of the livestream plan, a final decision is yet to be made.

It would be the first public execution in the US in almost a century.

The plan, which was announced by Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth last week, has been heavily criticised by politicians, academics and experts.

articles.title: K/DA Is Getting an Official Louis Vuitton Art Book Ahead of 'Start a Fire' Comeback
articles.body:
Riot Games has teamed up with fashion house Louis Vuitton on a K/DA Travel Book. The book’s reveal comes just after the League of Legends girl group announced their return from a six-year hiatus.

Tempo Point will collect new illustrations of the virtual girl group, envisioning “24 hours within the individual lives of K/DA members Ahri (vocalist), Akali (rapper), Evelynn (vocalist), and Kai’Sa (vocalist and lead dancer/choreographer).” A Standard edition and Collector’s edition will be released online and in select Louis Vuitton locations and bookstores on Friday, October 16.

First Look at Tempo Point - A K/DA Travel Book

The Louis Vuitton Travel Books are a series of premium artbooks, compiling images and illustrations from artists around the world. This particular addition to the collection will be available in two formats: a Standard Edition ($68 USD) and a Collector’s Large-Format Edition ($245 USD). Both editions feature the same artwork in six-color printing, collected in a cloth-bound hardcover book with a silk-screened cover.

Only 400 copies are being printed of the Collector's Edition, which will be available for purchase online on Louis Vuitton’s website , at Louis Vuitton stores, and in select bookstores. The Standard Edition will be available from the same places, and will also be shown off at the upcoming League of Legends Worlds 2026 Fan Fest event scheduled for November 12 to 14 in New York.

Select Louis Vuitton stores will also have limited-edition signed copies that come with an exclusive vinyl record. Only 30 total copies of this edition will be available.

While the Louis Vuitton of it all may seem a bit random, the French fashion house has actually been a consistent collaborator for Riot Games and the virtual girl group.

In 2019, the House served as the official Summoner’s Cup Trophy Trunk provider for the League Worlds Championship. Nicolas Ghesquière, the House’s Artistic Director of Women's Collections, has designed a number of skins for League of Legends, and the House dressed K/DA and guest artist Lexie Liu, who voiced Seraphine, throughout promotions for “MORE.”

K/DA, a virtual pop group which debuted with the single POP/STARS in 2018, just teased their first comeback since 2020. The new project was revealed with an image posted to K/DA social accounts , showing each members’ eyes and the tagline “Start a Fire.” The full project will be revealed on October 20.

articles.title: Pro Dota 2 Player Claims He Had to Play a Full Match in Front of Police Officers to Prove His Identity
articles.summary: A pro Dota 2 player is claiming he had to play a full Dota match in front of police officers to prove his identity. Thankfully, he had the sauce.
articles.body:
A pro Dota 2 player is claiming that he had to play a full Dota match in front of police officers to prove his identity.

According to Nuengnara "23savage" Teeramahanon, who currently plays hard carry for Xipto eSports, the team’s boot camp in Kuala Lumpur was raided by police earlier this week. In a post to Facebook on Tuesday, 23savage describes the police placing the team in handcuffs and confiscating their belongings.

The officers proceeded to interrogate the players about why they were in the city and whether they were really pro players. According to 23savage, one of the officers was familiar with Dota, and was willing to scroll the player’s Instagram for proof of his pro career.

A photo 23savage had recently posted of himself and popular Malaysian influencer Ms. Puiyi was, according to the post, somewhat acceptable evidence. Enough evidence, in fact, for the police officers to remove his handcuffs and test what really mattered: how good he is at defending the ancients.

23savage proceeded to start up a Dota match right in front of the police officers, dropping 32 kills as the hard carry Kez. The Dota player alleges that this was enough proof to convince the officers to let the team go, and also that they stole two jars of Nutella on their way out.

Commenters on the post quickly doubted 23savage’s claims, presuming the post to be a joke, but 23savage has been actively defending his story in the replies. Reddit users continue to doubt the hard carry player, while others jokingly claim 23savage’s story is saving Valve’s MOBA.

The incident doesn’t seem to have had much impact on Xipto, who have been climbing the ranks of SEA Dota. The team recently won the EPL SEA tournament without losing a single series, achieving an impressive 10-match win streak. The team’s full roster currently consists of 23savage (Carry), inYourdreaM (Mid), Fbz (Offlane), Q (Support), and Oli (Support), who are now competing for a spot in the DreamLeague Season 30 tournament .

Dota 2 itself has been seeing some notable player gains in 2026, having recently hit its peak player count since 2022 . The game continues to receive occasional patches and content updates, though Valve's focus is largely now on a new MOBA: Deadlock .

articles.title: 'I Just Sort of Disconnect' — Jeff Kaplan is Avoiding Overwatch at all Costs
articles.summary: Former Overwatch director Jeff Kaplan explained how he protects his psyche by completely avoiding online discussions and subreddits about Blizzard's hero shooter.
articles.body:
Former Overwatch director Jeff Kaplan explained how he protects his psyche by completely avoiding online discussions and subreddits about Blizzard's hero shooter.

If you’re a die-hard Overwatch player, you’re likely familiar with the name Jeff Kaplan. He was essentially the face of the game for years, endearing fans with his regular developer updates and memorable interactions with its fanbase.

After leaving Blizzard in 2021 , Kaplan founded his own game development studio and is currently working on an open world, action-survival shooter called The Legend of California. He has firmly put Overwatch behind him — to the point where he avoids interacting with it at all costs online.

Overwatch "The Reign of Talon" New Hero Images

“With Overwatch, I had a very almost clinical separation, knowing how the WoW thing had gone,” Kaplan said in a recent interview with GameSpot . “I’ve literally not played the game since April 2021.

“I don’t, for my own psyche, I don’t read the subreddits. After I said my goodbye to competitive Overwatch and the Overwatch subreddit, I never go back and read. I don’t watch YouTube [videos]. I don’t search for my name in Overwatch. I don’t search for Overwatch. I sort of just disconnect. I actually tell all the algorithms like, ‘Yeah, I’m not really interested in Overwatch anymore. I know you think I’m the Overwatch guy, but like, that’s just not for me anymore.'”

He told the outlet that it was surprisingly more painful for him to leave the World of Warcraft team to work on Overwatch than it was to put the hero shooter in his rear view, calling it a “training moment” for taking the next step in his career.

“WoW was who I was at that point,” he explained. “I worked every minute, every waking minute, on WoW. If I wasn’t working on WoW, I was playing WoW. And every time I played WoW, I had this notepad next to the desk that I’d be filling out to walk in the next morning and go, ‘These are all the things we need to change.’ It was kind of shocking in a very negative emotional way to step away from WoW, because it was such a part of who I was and how I identified. It was who I was as a game developer.”

After learning the hard way that the games he worked on didn’t belong to him, but were instead an IP under Blizzard’s ownership, it was easier for him to move forward.

“Overwatch happened. I was a part of it. There’s a group there now, and Overwatch is now about them. Both the players and the developers, that’s their Overwatch now. They’re making it, they own it, they play it. I’m onto this new thing, and that’s where I’m at in my life,” he said.

Kaplan hasn’t shied away from sharing his thoughts on the current gaming industry since making his exit from Blizzard almost half a decade ago. Most recently, he had some harsh words for players who complain about games they’ll never actually play.

"If a game comes out, and you don't want to play it, and you've never played it? Shut the f*** up. No one cares,” he said.

And in March, he revealed the reason why he actually left Blizzard behind, describing a specific meeting that he called “the biggest f*** you moment I had in my career.”

articles.title: Melquisedek Menezes é nomeado adjunto da Saúde de Boa Vista e Major assume Cargo de vereador | G1

articles.summary: Melquisedek deixa o cargo de vereador uma semana após assumir a vaga de Deyvid Carneiro (União Brasil), que teve o mandato cassado pelo TRE-RR por crime eleitoral.
articles.body:
Major Emmanuel tomou posse como vereador de Boa Vista — Foto: Reprodução/ Instagram

O vereador Melquisedek da Silva Menezes (União Brasil) foi nomeado como adjunto da Secretaria Municipal de Saúde de Boa Vista nesta sexta-feira (16). Após deixar o cargo na Câmara Municipal, o Major Emmanuel (PL) assume a cadeira como vereador.

Melquisedek tomou posse como vereador no dia 9 de outubro, após o Tribunal Regional de Roraima (TRE-RR) cassar o mandato de Deyvid Carneiro, do mesmo partido, por crime eleitoral. A nomeação como novo secretário adjunto foi publicada no Diário Oficial de Boa Vista.

A Câmara Municipal diplomou o Major Emmanuel, 1º suplente do União Brasil. O novo vererador da capital é piloto de caça da Força Aérea Brasileira (FAB) e criador de conteúdo digital.

Emmanuel de Oliveira Novaes, de 40 anos, é natural de São José dos Campos, em São Paulo. Nas eleições deste, ano ele se candidatou a deputado federal pelo Partido Liberal (PL), mas não foi eleito. Em 2024, foi candidato a vereador em Boa Vista e, em 2022, disputou como deputado estadual, também sem sucesso.

Melquisedek da Silva Menezes (União Brasil), de 49 anos, é engenheiro e técnico de enfermagem . Ele iniciou a trajetória política em 2018, segundo dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE). Naquele ano, foi candidato a deputado estadual pelo Partido Trabalhista Brasileiro (PTB), mas ficou como suplente.

Em 2020, foi eleito vereador de Boa Vista pelo Partido Social Liberal (PSL). Em 2022, filiou-se ao União Brasil e disputou novamente uma vaga na Assembleia Legislativa de Roraima (ALE-RR), mas ficou como suplente.

Em 2024, concorreu à reeleição para a Câmara Municipal de Boa Vista, mas ficou como suplente, posição que ocupava até a retotalização dos votos após a cassação de Deyvid Carneiro. Em 2026, disputaria uma vaga de deputado estadual, mas teve o pedido de renúncia à candidatura aceito pela Justiça Eleitoral em setembro.

India's teenage cricket sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi had a witty message for photographers eager to film him at the airport, reminding them not to compromise their safety while chasing social media content. Addressing the athletes, the Prime Minister encouraged them to visit schools and their hometowns to inspire young people through their experiences. He emphasised that even a brief interaction with a sportsperson could motivate a child to pursue athletics. Modi further highlighted how sports instil discipline, resilience and perseverance, helping individuals overcome setbacks and remain committed to their goals.
