articles.title: Dodgers 2026 offseason roster breakdown
articles.summary: The Dodgers 2026 season has ended, so it’s now time to focus on what figures to be a tumultuous offseason with the Major League Baseball collective bargainin...
articles.body:
The Dodgers 2026 season has ended , so it's now time to focus on what figures to be a tumultuous offseason with the Major League Baseball collective bargaining agreement expiring on December 1. But before we get to the lockout, there are still roster decisions to be made, so let's see how the Dodgers look at the start of their offseason.

The season ended with six Dodgers players on the 60-day injured list and thus 46 players on the 40-man roster . The morning after the World Series ends, that number will be reduced to 37, with nine players set for free agency.

Because Tarik Skubal was traded midseason, he is ineligible to be tendered a qualifying offer, so the Dodgers won't receive draft pick compensation should he sign elsewhere. Same for Kris Bubic and Eric Lauer, but they weren't going to get a qualifying offer anyway. Miguel Rojas retired after 13 seasons as a player , and already has a spot waiting in the Dodgers front office, with a focus on player development.

The qualifying offer is a one-year offer, derived from the average of the top 125 salaries in the league that year. This offseason's qualifying offer will be $23.15 million, per Joel Sherman of the New York Post , up 5.11 percent from $22.025 million last year.

The Dodgers have no player or club options heading into the offseason, but let's first look at the players under contract.

The salaries above are the amounts paid in the year in question. Several players have deferred salaries , most notably Shohei Ohtani, who for each season of his contract is paid $2 million, with the other $68 million deferred 10 years down the road .

Per the collective bargaining agreement, the present value of the deferred salary for a season must be fully funded by the second July 1 following said season. So for the $68 million earned by Ohtani in 2026 that will be paid in 2036 must be funded by July 1, 2028. Payroll for competitive balance tax purposes accounts for all deferrals, converting them into net present value and averaged over the life of the contract. For Ohtani, his CBT payroll number is just over $46 million.

Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed a 12-year, $325 million contract prior to the 2024 season . He received all of his $50 million signing bonus in 2024, and lower salaries in the first three years of the deal, hence the $12 million salary in 2026. That bumps up to $26 million for each season from 2027-29. The right-hander can opt out of his contract after either the 2029 and 2031 seasons or 2031 and 2033, depending on whether or not he experiences certain injuries and misses a certain amount of time.

Will Smith signed a 10-year contract in 2024 that runs through 2033 . In both 2026 and 2027, his salary is $13 million, with $5 million deferred, with those deferrals paid annual from 2034-2043.

Mookie Betts prior to the 2020 season signed a 12-year, $365 million extension that started in 2021 and runs through 2032. His contract fits the rubric of many Dodgers contracts to follow, with a large signing bonus ($65 million, 17.8 percent of the total) as well as a sizable amount of deferred salary ($115 million, 31.5 percent). For both 2026 and 2027, Betts has a $25 million salary, of which $10 million is deferred, plus he gets $5 million of his signing bonus, for a total paid of $20 million in each of these two seasons.

Kyle Tucker's four-year, $240 million contract included a $64 million signing bonus, of which $10 million will be paid on February 1, 2027. His salary for 2027 is $54 million, minus $10 million deferred. He can opt out of the final two years of his contract after the 2027 season.

Blake Snell's five-year, $182 million contract included a $52 million signing bonus that was all paid in 2025. The remaining $26 million per year includes $13.2 million deferred each season, leaving Snell with $12.8 million per year. Snell's contract also includes a conditional 2030 club option with $10 million depending should he suffer a qualifying injury.

Tommy Edman signed a five-year, $74 million contract ahead of 2025 that included a $17 million signing bonus already paid. His salary in both 2026 and 2027 is $12.25 million, of which $6.25 million is deferred annually. The Dodgers hold a $13 million club option on Edman for 2030 that includes a $3 million buyout.

Edwin Díaz last December broke his own record for highest average annual salary by a relief pitcher with his three-year, $69 million contract . In 2027, Díaz has a $23 million salary, of which $4.5 million is deferred.

Tanner Scott's four-year, $72 million contract runs through 2028 . His $20 million signing bonus is split evenly over the four years of the contract. Scott in 2027 has a $15 million salary, of which $5.25 million is deferred, plus $5 million of his signing bonus.

Freddie Freeman in 2027 enters the final year of his six-year, $162 million contract . He'll get his $27 million, minus $12 million deferred salary.

Tyler Glasnow is under contract for one more year at $30 million in 2027 . Then in 2028 he has a player option worth $21,562,500, but if he declines that player option the Dodgers have a club option worth $30 million.

Teoscar Hernández has a $14.5 million salary for 2027 , of which $8 million is deferred, and the Dodgers have a $15 million club option for 2028 with a $6.5 million buyout. That's $21 million in guaranteed money should the Dodgers try to trade Hernández and open up an outfield spot for Josue De Paula.

Max Muncy had a base salary of $10 million in 2026 , then played in a career-high 149 games and batted 561 times. Incentives in his contract added $2.25 million to his base salary in 2026 ($15,000 for every plate appearance from 401 to 550), and also added $3.75 million to his 2027 base salary ($20,000 for every 2026 PA from 401 to 500, $35,000 for every 2026 PA from 501 to 550). Muncy's contract originally called for a $7 million base salary in 2027 (now $10.75 million), and the Dodgers have a $10 million club option in 2028 with a $3 million buyout.

Hyeseong Kim is under contract for $3.75 million in 2027 , and the Dodgers have a two-year club option for 2028-29 at $5 million in each season, with a $1.5 million buyout if declined.

All told, the 14 players under contract have a total competitive balance payroll of roughly $339.5 million for 2027. The caveat here is we don't know if the competitive balance tax will remain in the current format with a new collective bargaining agreement, or if it will even exist at all. But that's what the Dodgers have on the books for now.

The salary projections above are from MLB Trade Rumors . We'll dive deeper into each case in the offseason, just like we did last January . But for now, if those projections hold, that would add six players for a guaranteed $12.9 million. Added to the players already under contract, that's 18 players for about $351.4 million for competitive balance tax purposes.

Andy Pages is eligible for arbitration as a Super Two player, a player among the top 22 percent in service time for players with at least two but not yet three years of service time. It takes 172 days to accrue a full year of service time. Alex Call was a Super Two player last offseason.

If this were a normal offseason, the date for players and teams to exchange salaries for arbitration would be Friday, January 8, 2027. But MLB will almost certainly be in a lockout by then. In the 2022 season, some salary arbitration hearings were held well after the regular season began.

The major league minimum salary in 2026 was $780,000. The 2027 minimum salary hasn't yet been determined, but will certainly be a part of the next collective bargaining agreement. The 22.7-percent raise from 2021 to 2022 (the first year of the current CBA) was the largest such negotiated increase in nearly two decades.

Minimum salary raise in first year of recent CBAs

2021-22 : $570,500 to $700,000 (22.7 percent)

2016-17 : $507,500 to $535,000 (5.4 percent)

2011-12 : $414,000 to $480,000 (15.9 percent)

2006-07: $327,000 to $380,000 (16.2 percent)

2002-03: $200,000 to $300,000 (50 percent)

October28-November 1: At 6 a.m. PT the morning after the World Series ends, players with at least six years of service time and/or at the completion of their contracts become free agents.

November 2-6: Five days after the World Series ends is the deadline for teams to make qualifying offers to players. It's also the end of the "quiet period" of free agency, during which players can only sign with their former team.

November 17: 1 p.m. PT deadline for players to accept qualifying offers

November 17: Reserve lists filed (prospects added to 40-man roster)

Josue De Paula would have been added to the 40-man roster by that November 17 deadline to avoid getting plucked in the Rule 5 Draft, but he was already called up in September. Players drafted or signed at age 19 or older in 2023 or players drafted or signed at 18 or younger in 2022 are newly eligible for the Rule 5 Draft this December. Dodgers top pitching prospect Christian Zazueta, signed by the Cubs out of Mexico in 2022, will need to be added to the 40-man roster by November 17. Zazueta has won the Branch Rickey Award as the Dodgers minor league pitcher of the year for two years running , and he just turned 22 last week.

Another potential addition is Jackson Ferris, a former top Dodgers pitching prospect drafted by the Cubs in 2022 who struggled for most of 2026 before a sublime final five weeks .

The collective bargaining agreement expires at 8:59 p.m. PT on December 1, after which the owners will lock out the players. But there's still about a month that could be quite busy on the hot stove before the sport gets shut down for the winter.

articles.title: Detroit Lions Place 3 Players on Injured Reserve
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions placed Tom Kennedy, Ben Bartch and Devin White on injured reserve, opening three roster spots ahead of the Packers game.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions made three significant roster moves Friday, and while the immediate news involves more injuries, the bigger story could be who is preparing to return.

Detroit has placed wide receiver Tom Kennedy, offensive lineman Ben Bartch, and linebacker Devin White on injured reserve , officially opening three spots on its 53-man roster.

The transactions come during the Lions' Week 6 bye, giving general manager Brad Holmes an opportunity to reshape the roster before Detroit's October 25 showdown with the Green Bay Packers.

And two important reinforcements could be on the way.

Detroit Lions Place Three Players on Injured Reserve

The Lions' latest roster transactions mean Kennedy, Bartch, and White must each miss at least four games before becoming eligible to return.

Here's where things stand with all three players:

Tom Kennedy (WR/Returner): Suffered an MCL injury against Arizona in Week 5 and will undergo season-ending surgery.

Ben Bartch (OL): Has been sidelined by a foot injury since appearing in Detroit's Week 2 matchup against Buffalo.

Devin White (LB): Suffered a broken forearm against Arizona and requires surgery. A return later this season remains possible.

Kennedy's absence creates a particularly important special teams vacancy. Detroit recently added veteran return specialist DeAndre Carter to its practice squad, making him one possible candidate to take over those responsibilities.

White's injury is another setback for Detroit's defense, although the Lions have additional depth at linebacker. Bartch's absence, meanwhile, further reduces the team's offensive line flexibility.

But there's a potentially encouraging development hidden within these transactions.

Brian Branch and Cade Mays Could Be Next

With three roster spots now available, Detroit has room to activate two players fans have been eagerly waiting to see.

Safety Brian Branch and center Cade Mays are both practicing during their return evaluation windows, and each could be available when the Lions return from their bye.

As we previously reported when both players returned to practice , Branch has been recovering from an Achilles injury, while Mays has been sidelined by a fractured wrist.

Branch's return would be particularly important for a secondary that has struggled with injuries and inconsistent coverage. His versatility would give defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard another experienced option as Detroit prepares to face Jordan Love and the Packers.

Juice Scruggs has performed exceptionally well while filling in at center, meaning head coach Dan Campbell will have a decision to make once Mays is healthy enough to play.

We also highlighted Campbell's Week 7 target for both players , although neither has been officially activated.

What Happens With Detroit's Third Open Roster Spot?

If Branch and Mays occupy two of the three available spots, Holmes will still have another opening to address a roster need.

One logical possibility involves Detroit's return game.

Carter brings extensive NFL experience handling punts and kickoffs, and Kennedy's season-ending injury gives the Lions a legitimate reason to add another specialist to the active roster.

However, Carter isn't the only option. Detroit could evaluate its existing practice squad receivers before deciding who provides the best combination of return ability and offensive depth.

The team also has the flexibility to address its secondary, where additional depth could prove valuable even if Branch returns.

The important point is that none of those corresponding moves has been announced.

With the Lions on their bye week, Detroit doesn't need to rush into filling every vacancy. The coaching staff can evaluate recovering players and determine which additions will best prepare the team for its return.

As the injured-reserve transactions were confirmed Friday , the three openings created an opportunity for Detroit to welcome back important contributors without immediately releasing healthy players.

For a team sitting at 3-2 and preparing for a crucial stretch of NFC North games, that's a valuable bit of flexibility.

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition intercepts drones as Egypt weighs sending help
articles.summary: Forces intercepted and destroyed four drones over Saudi Arabia’s Riyadh, Eastern Province and southern region.
articles.body:
The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis has said it intercepted and destroyed four drones over Riyadh and other regions, the latest in a wave of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia’s airports and oil facilities.

“We intercepted and destroyed four drones over the past few hours in the regions of Riyadh, the Eastern Province, and the South,” coalition spokesperson Major-General Turki al-Maliki said on Saturday.

He also posted footage of what he described as the air force intercepting cruise missiles and drones and striking ballistic missile launchers belonging to the Houthis.

Riyadh’s King Khalid airport has come under at least 20 attacks – including one last week that killed 13 people – since the fighting between the Houthi rebels and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government flared in July.

On Thursday, at least five people were killed in missile strikes near the presidential palace in Aden, the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognised government. It blamed the Houthis for the attack.

On Friday, the Yemeni government said the Houthis fired two missiles at Aden’s airport , while government forces said they had advanced in Marib province, northeast of Sanaa.

Saudi Arabia is backing a government counteroffensive, known as Dawn of Yemen, and has carried out air strikes on the Houthis, including on an oil facility in Sanaa.

Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi said on Saturday he was willing to “carry out any measure to protect” Saudi Arabia should the kingdom ask.

Egypt was not looking to intervene in regional wars, el-Sisi said, but it was “inconceivable” for Cairo to stand by while Saudi Arabia was harmed.

“I’m not talking about fighting anyone or attacking anyone. We are speaking only about defence,” he said.

Egypt’s parliament is holding an emergency session on Sunday at the president’s request.

Saudi Arabia has accused Iran of encouraging the Houthis’ escalation. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, meanwhile, said Tehran supported a “comprehensive political process as the only practical and sustainable way to resolve” the conflict.

Several embassies in Saudi Arabia have restricted travel and warned citizens not to use airports.

The Saudi Ministry of Education extended remote learning for students in Riyadh and nearby Diriyah in light of the recent Houthi attacks.

articles.title: How The Traitors' music plays with your emotions
articles.summary: It's not just treachery and villainy - the soundtrack for Traitors helps set the show's campy tone.
articles.body:
Suspicion, intrigue, treachery, Claudia Winkleman. The Traitors has it all.

But the shadowiest of the show's shadowy secrets is its music.

Have you ever noticed how the soundtrack manipulates your perception? A sinister orchestral flourish hints at a double cross. A cheeky chord injects humour into a kitchen conflab.

As ever, though, you shouldn't trust what happens in the castle. The music can provide emphasis or act as misdirection, all at the producers' behest.

Duplicity was baked into the music from the beginning.

"I remember the BBC was quite reluctant to even think about a show with murder as a main feature, so I knew I didn't want the music to go really dark," says Sam Watts, who composed the opening theme and much of the incidental score (but is not responsible for the show's haunting cover versions of well-known pop songs... more on those later).

Watts, who had previously worked on Planet Earth and The Sarah Jane Adventures, pitched to work on the programme with only a basic idea of the set-up. It was only when he learned Winkleman was the host that he settled on his approach.

"They sent me a little shot they'd done of the opening with Claudia and the castle. That's when I knew it was going to be a bit camp and high drama and all the glorious things that Claudia brings to the show. So I just went with that - dark but fun."

For the title sequence, the 44-year-old wanted something memorable. As a kid, his favourite song was Bernard Hoffer's gloriously over-the-top Thundercats theme , so that's the level he aspired to.

"I was trying to write something that signified the show was starting, so that people would run in from making their cup of tea in the kitchen to watch it.

"And I wanted a memorable melody that people could hum, because it helps with the identity of the show."

The Traitors theme is "one of the biggest pieces of music I've ever written", he says, recorded with a full orchestra and overdubbed with dozens of electronic elements to create a heightened, hyperreal atmosphere.

That bled into the 20 or so other pieces Watts wrote, which also appear in dozens of international spin-offs.

The Celebrity Traitors connections that might surprise you

What role would you play in the Traitors castle? Take our quiz to find out

The idea, he says, is that the whole hour feels like a film trailer, with viewers permanently waiting for the psychological pressure chamber to explode.

To achieve that, he employed several techniques of trailer music - most notably the " Braam ", a klaxon-like punctuation mark invented for Christopher Nolan's Inception (see video for a fuller exploration).

Show producer Sarah Fay took that concept and amplified it. "We wanted to just supersize it and make it feel like a drama, not like your usual reality [show]," she said in a rare interview with Metro when the first civilian series aired in 2022.

"We wanted to make it feel like that edge-of-your-seat cinematic drama with, you know, elements of Succession, and we wanted it to feel like Knives Out when you get into the castle!"

To achieve that, she commissioned additional music from film trailer composers, including Hans Zimmer's company Bleeding Fingers. But she also sprinkled in a handful of creepy cover versions.

Some became instant classics - such as a sinister spin on Britney Spears' Toxic , or a version of Tears For Fears' Mad World seemingly broadcast on a tannoy from Hades.

They're so integral to The Traitors' aesthetic that it might surprise you to learn they weren't recorded specifically for the show.

Both examples were created by German writer-producers 2wei.

Based in Hamburg, they had no idea their music had appeared in The Traitors until friends in the UK messaged them in excitement.

"We were just flipping out," says 2wei's Simon Heeger. "It's completely different to how we ever thought it would be used."

Heeger founded 2wei, pronounced "zwei", in 2016 with his old college friend Christian Vorländer.

They had both spent time in LA working on advertisements and (stop me if you're sensing a theme here) film trailers, before moving home to build a music production empire.

"Christian worked on the Mad Max soundtrack, which is really known for the big drums and the orchestral scale – and that was really the starting point of our sound," says Heeger.

"Whenever you hear big epic drums with an orchestral sound and maybe a female vocal on top of it, it's usually something we had our fingers in."

Their big break came with a stormy reworking of Destiny's Child's Survivor, which featured in the trailer to Alicia Vikander's Tomb Raider .

Since then, their music has appeared in films like Wonder Woman and video games such as League of Legends. In The Traitors, original 2wei songs like Blindside now feature alongside their covers (other producers, including SYML and Damned Anthem also contribute songs to the show).

Heeger says their background in commercials makes the music perfectly suited to the show's slippery skullduggery.

"In adverts, you only have a few seconds to convey a certain emotion and, especially in Traitors, where there are cliffhangers and moments that you don't expect, you need music that comes to the point right away but still has a boldness to it.

"It's a sweet spot, and it's not easy to convey, but every now and then it works quite well."

On Spotify, there are hundreds of playlists dedicated to the programme's background music. Some are tailored to murder mystery parties and Halloween events. Others compile more sedate moments under labels like "gentle tension" or "chill elder emo watching Traitors".

But never forget: the soundtrack is playing a deceitful game of its own.

"A lot of my music has a wink in it and, for The Traitors, it's a little silly and slightly over the top," says Watts.

"I think it helps the nastier side of things - the murder, the plotting - feel a bit more fun."

articles.title: Lady Glenconner recalls being told off by Queen at Holkham Hall
articles.summary: Lady Glenconner says there are "so many memories wherever I go at Holkham", her ancestral estate.
articles.body:
One of Princess Margaret's former ladies in waiting recalls being told off by a nine-year-old Queen Elizabeth II for riding a tricycle indoors at her Norfolk stately home.

Lady Glenconner, who has known the Royal Family all her life, said it was a privilege growing up at Holkham Hall, which is her family's ancestral estate.

Now aged 94, she remembers riding tricycles as a young child with the Queen's younger sister, Princess Margaret - and being chided by the future monarch.

"We weren't meant to be there at all, going round and round, and down the steps of the Marble Hall came the Queen... she looked at us and she said 'Margaret, Anne, very very naughty, what are you doing'?" said Lady Glenconner.

"Princess Margaret and I whirled round the hall one more time and we shot off on our tricycles screaming with laughter," she added.

In an interview with the BBC Radio Norfolk's Louise Hulland, she said: "I sometimes look at people going round Holkham and you'd never know the Queen aged nine went down the steps you are walking down.

"There are so many memories wherever I go at Holkham."

The history of Holkham Hall dates back to 1609 when Sir Edward Coke - later Earl of Leicester - purchased Neales Manor in Holkham Parish and founded the Holkham Estate.

Lady Glenconner's father, Major Thomas Coke, the fifth Earl, was equerry to the Queen's father, King George VI. He opened Holkham Hall - which remains the ancestral home of the Earl of Leicester - to visitors for the first time in 1950.

Lady Glenconner said she remembered that during the war "garden boys" would stoke heaters in the estate's growing houses at night to make the exotic fruit ripen quicker.

She said photograph albums had helped keep the memories alive and been "invaluable" to her books.

Her latest memoir, Trunks and Tiaras, transports readers from grand houses and royal tours to hidden corners of the world sharing the people, places and adventures that have shaped her life.

In 1971 she was appointed as a lady-in-waiting to Princess Margaret, a role she believed she was trusted with for her discreetness.

On 7 November, she will return to Holkham for a signing of her latest memoir, however, she has continued to frequent the home since growing up.

She recently took her grandson to see an opera performance held at the hall.

She said: "It was very hot and the deer started to come out from under the trees and I just thought it's paradise at the moment. It doesn't happen very often in this life but it was just perfect and I just thought how lucky I am to be brought up at Holkham and it was great.

"I said to my grandson to enjoy and remember this moment because it does not often happen," she said.

articles.title: Why baseball teams party so hard and so often in October
articles.summary: Every major US sport has multi-round post season schedules, but none of them party like the teams in MLB.
articles.body: Toward the end of every regular season, if it’s been a good one, the Boston Red Sox will receive a special package from one of their kit suppliers: 100 pairs of goggles. It’s an unusual gift for a baseball team, but each playoff round brings another shipment of 100 more pairs of eyewear until they reach the World Series. The reason? Champagne sprayed at point-blank range at high velocity into the face will sting your eyes, and baseball players tend to do a lot of that when they’re winning. Every major US sport has multi-round postseason schedules, but none of them party like MLB teams. Locker room celebrations in the NFL tend to be subdued until the Super Bowl, and since hockey players are famously superstitious, popping bottles early is practically verboten in the NHL; the Stanley Cup is all that really matters. Clubhouse manager Tom McLaughlin has spent over 40 years with the Red Sox, and he says he’s lost track of how many celebrations he’s been involved in, but he counts them in the dozens. He told CNN Sports it was “pretty tame” when he started in the ‘80s, when the postseason was much shorter, but the back end of the season now can feel like one enormous bender for the most successful teams. Clinched a playoff spot? Party. Successfully navigate the wildcard round? Let’s get wild. Made it through the Divisional Round? Get another round in. Won the Championship Series? We’re going on a spree. By the time a baseball club wins the World Series, let’s just say that the celebration will not be their first rodeo. Everyone will have had plenty of practice. One of McLaughlin’s jobs is to procure the booze. Another is to try and keep the bubbly off everybody’s personal belongings, the furniture, TVs and audio equipment. Look closely at any video footage in the aftermath of a clinching victory and you’ll see protective plastic sheeting everywhere. It resembles the “kill room” in the TV show “Dexter.” It takes two hours to get all the safeguarding stuff in place, and if it looks like things are going sideways on the diamond, the staff will be waiting, mid-ladder, for the call to rip all the plastic down. For a series win, such protection is essential. “That first hour is intense,” McLaughlin told CNN Sports. “It’s crazy.” “Earn the burn” Expensive bottles of Moët & Chandon or Dom Pérignon are revved up in the revelry and everyone and everything gets soaked. “It’s very wet. It’s sticky. If you have like a paper cut or a scrape, it’s getting in there,” explained former slugger Curtis Granderson to CNN. “It turns into like a playful water gun fight. Everybody gets their ammunition with their bottle of champagne, and then you’re shaking it up to make it just amped up, ready to go. And whether you’re spraying it to hit the ceiling, hit a couch, hit a teammate, hit a reporter, do it to yourself. Everything is a target within the locker room.” Targeting somebody for a soaking is a sign of respect. After playing a key role in the Cleveland Guardians’ Wild Card series comeback against the Chicago White Sox, Steven Kwan was barely able to speak with a reporter in the clubhouse. “I mean, no! God, no!” he gasped as suds were poured all over his head. “It’s so cold! I feel like I’m being targeted right now. I’m in the ring. I’m trying to survive, but this is a ton of fun.” Granderson recalled that of the 12 to 15 clubhouse celebrations he was involved in, he doesn’t remember drinking any of the champagne. “I think I was mostly spraying it,” he said. “It was around my face and mouth, so I tasted it. I didn’t actually pour it up and drink it though.” Granderson says he treasures some of the goggles from those celebrations in his trophy cabinet, but others prefer to engage all five of their senses during the celebration. “A teammate of mine, Michael Cuddyer, he was the one saying you got to ‘earn the burn,’” explained Granderson. “He would always go with no goggles because he loved the fact that it burned his eyes. Because, to get a chance to do that meant you were doing something well.” Sometimes, it’s not just the booze. McLaughlin says he remembers the New York Yankees celebrating a series victory at Fenway in the ‘90s and food, milk and yogurt were thrown around. They even dragged the hose out of the shower for good measure. “The Yankees of the ‘90s did not get cheated when they had fun,” he said, acknowledging the scale of the mess they had to clean up between the end of the party and sunrise. “If you were in a hotel lobby, it would be a lot different,” he laughed. “I’m sure the police would be involved.” Making their mark Every year, as the postseason approaches, a carpet-cleaning company in Boston knows to stand by; if a series is clinched, they’ll be called in for a shampooing assignment at 2 a.m. The clubhouse managers try to protect as much of the property as possible, but there is only so much they can do. “No matter how much you clean it, it smells horrible for days,” McLaughlin said, adding that the ceiling tiles turn brown, almost black, and must be replaced. So why does baseball find these celebrations so irresistible? McLaughlin ponders the question: “I don’t know where it came from, I really don’t, I wish I had the magic answer.” He begins thinking out loud, recalling the players and teams that he’s seen redecorate his clubhouse so enthusiastically over the years. Eventually he settles on the idea that success can be so fleeting, “You could be a player that came up and only had an impact in one game – you might never be in the Major Leagues again. So, I think when you have the opportunity to celebrate, to appreciate where you’re at, why not?” Baseball is a high-pressure psychological game where the difference between success and failure is razor-thin, and the players are trained to keep their emotions in check. Teams are tight-knit, spending practically every moment together from Spring Training through October in what can be described as a 162-game marathon. So perhaps it makes sense to view a party after clinching a pennant or a place in the postseason as more of a release of all the pent-up stress, a relief that the season wasn’t in vain. Sure, you might be celebrating another triumph in a week’s time, but the end of the road might come just as quickly, and you may never see some of your teammates again. Granderson doesn’t believe that repeat celebrations diminish the significance of the ultimate prize, the World Series. “It’s like birthdays,” he mused. “We have our first birthday – is that one more important than the 16th? Is that one more important than the 21st? Is that one more important than the 50th? They all have their special moments.” McLaughlin agrees with the sentiment, adding a caveat. “The big thing is at the end of each series when you win, you get a hat and T-shirt on the field that says division champ, American (League) champ; people want those so bad,” he said. “But when you get one that says world champ, you don’t even know where the other ones are.” However, there might be one exception. In 2004, the Red Sox swept the St. Louis Cardinals 4-0 to win their first World Series since 1918, ending the so-called 86-year Curse of the Bambino. But McLaughlin recalls it wasn’t the biggest celebration of that postseason. In fact, it was in the previous round, when they clawed their way back from 3-0 down against their fiercest rivals, those pesky Yankees, and clinched the series in New York. It was the first, and remains the only time an MLB club has dug themselves out of such a deep hole. That was the party everyone remembers in 2004. That was also the season David Ortiz says that he introduced the idea of wearing the protective goggles to his Red Sox teammates. Now, when any baseball player looks back on the best nights of their careers, they’ll hopefully remember how good it all looked, even if they needed goggles to see it.

Roger's opening speech. If the mini-season follows the pattern of the Simpsons season last year, expect a themed map, a mini Battle Pass, and plenty of cosmetics. Sprites are also expected to continue, based on speculation, though nothing is confirmed.The teaser chest, the datamined files, and consistent leaks all point toward an anime-flavored mini-season starting November 1. articles.title: Now, UG students can change major subjects too in second year
articles.summary: DAVV lets UG students in BA, BSc, BCom and other courses change their major subject when entering second year, starting the 2025-26 session.
articles.body: Indore: Students who realise after their first year of college that they have chosen the wrong major subject will now get a chance to start afresh without changing their degree programme. Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya (DAVV) has allowed undergraduate students to switch their major subject while moving to the second year, starting this academic session.The facility covers BA, BSc, BCom and other undergraduate programmes. Students who completed their first year in the 2025-26 academic session can change their major while taking admission to the second year. The students of this year’s batch will be able to exercise the option next year.Under the revised arrangement, a BSc student pursuing biotechnology can opt for microbiology, botany or another available subject as the major. Similarly, a BA student who chose economics in the first year can switch to history, Hindi, political science or another subject offered by the college.Until now, students could change their minor subjects but were not allowed to switch their major. As a result, those who found the syllabus difficult, lost interest in their chosen subject or performed poorly often had to continue with the same subject throughout their undergraduate course.Examination controller Ashesh Tiwari said the flexibility would help students avoid being stuck with an unsuitable subject. Poor performance in a major can affect overall graduation results and leave students with fewer choices while applying for postgraduate courses.The demand for such flexibility has been significant. Around 500 to 1,000 students have been approaching colleges or DAVV every year seeking permission to change their major subject.The provision follows the implementation of the National Education Policy in 2021, under which the major subject plays a central role in determining a student’s undergraduate degree. articles.title: How a grass fire at a Canadian military base killed four soldiers
articles.summary: Cause of grass fire remains unknown as PM Carney calls it one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canadian military.
articles.body:
On Saturday morning, Canadian military officials at a base in Alberta province observed a grass fire that appeared sufficiently contained, allowing soldiers to conduct live-fire combat training. Then, the officials say, the wind shifted.

In less than a minute, Canadian soldiers went from training drills to being engulfed in flames, said Major-General Wade Rutland, describing the incident that killed four soldiers and injured 39 people, 19 of them critically.

“The fire was a kilometre away when the wind shifted. That is not normal for a fire to move a kilometre in 36 seconds,” Rutland said at a news conference in Edmonton, the capital of Alberta, on Sunday.

While the cause of the grass blaze remains unknown, Prime Minister Mark Carney described the incident as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada’s military on domestic soil.

So how did the grass fire spread so fast, and why is this base significant?

A grass fire spreads through dry grass, weeds, shrubs and other low-growing vegetation. Unlike forest fires that burn through trees and woodland, grass fires spread across open fields, grasslands and plains.

They can move exceptionally quickly because dry grass ignites easily and provides a continuous source of fuel, and wind can play a pivotal role in how the fire develops.

Strong winds push flames rapidly across open terrain, change their direction with little warning, and carry burning embers ahead of the main fire, potentially igniting new fires.

The uncertainty of winds makes grass fires difficult to predict and contain, particularly in dry conditions.

They may burn for a shorter time than a forest fire, and while they are easier to contain, the speed at which they can spread in dry conditions can make them lethal.

Grass fires can start naturally but can also be ignited by human activities, such as discarded cigarettes or equipment sparks.

The fire spread on Saturday afternoon during high-intensity combat training involving Charlie Company of the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia’s Canadian Light Infantry, at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright in Alberta, western Canada, about 210km (130 miles) southeast of Edmonton.

The area lies in the prairies, a landscape of wide, open grasslands, rolling plains and scattered groves of trees. The base is also one of the Canadian Army’s largest training centres and a key facility for preparing troops for operational deployment.

About 84 soldiers were split between a grenade range and an area where they practised attacks on simulated enemy positions. The fire swept into the second training area.

Rutland said investigators would examine whether the wind drove the fire towards the soldiers or whether flames spread unseen through vegetation before suddenly overtaking them.

Large areas of Alberta were hit by a windstorm, with gusts up to 100km/h (62mph). The winds toppled trees, sent signs flying and pushed flames beyond the base into surrounding rural areas.

The fire also disrupted advance voting ahead of Monday’s referendum on whether Alberta should begin a process that could lead to independence from Canada.

On Sunday, the Canadian media reported that the fire could have worsened after a gas facility was struck during a live firing exercise. However, the military later clarified that investigators do not believe any explosions were caused by oil or gas infrastructure.

Global News, a Canadian publication, reported that an armed forces memo obtained by it noted the fire risk was assessed as low for the scheduled live-ammunition exercise, greenlighting soldiers to train.

However, Environment Canada had issued a strong-wind warning earlier that day, forecasting gusts of up to 100km/h in parts of Alberta.

The memo also noted that blazes jumped a fire guard and spread outside the base, forcing the evacuation of one family home.

“During training, a grass fire ignited, and strong winds caused the fire to spread rapidly and shift direction; the fire shifted toward the personnel on the range and overtook their admin area,” the memo states.

Global News reported that the memo warned that the situation was “fluid” and the casualty figures “may change over time with ongoing assessments” of status.

The Wainwright base is one of the country’s largest and most used military facilities, especially for training soldiers. It spans 609sq km (235sq miles) and is home to 25 weapons ranges.

During the final months of World War II and for several months in 1946, the base was used as an internment centre for German prisoners of war.

articles.body:
In the wake of K/DA’s Firestarter comeback , Secretlab has revealed a new gaming furniture collection themed after the virtual girl group.

The collection features new special-edition designs for two of Secretlab’s most popular products: the Titan Evo gaming chair and the Magnus Pro gaming desk. Both battlestation items are decorated with burgundy flames and this era’s K/DA insignia, including symbols for each member: Kai'Sa, Ahri, Akali, and Evelynn.

The full Secretlab x K/DA Firestarter collection is now available for purchase on the Secretlab site with optional add-ons and multiple sizes. The K/DA edition Titan EVO starts at $644 , while the flaming Magnus Pro desk starts at $978 .

Secretlab x K/DA Firestarter Collection Now Available

The new K/DA Firestarter collection is joining Secretlab's ridiculously long list of League of Legends-themed peripherals , including two existing collections for the girl group's previous eras.

The base model of the Secretlab Titan Evo is one of our favorite gaming chairs on the market. The racing-style chair sports an adjustable L-Adapt lumbar support system and a sizable “waterfall edge” seat design to improve blood flow. IGN’s reviewer, Chris Coke, spent two years with it as his main gaming chair to offer deeper insight, and found it “be the all-around best option, balancing ergonomics, style, and features that have since changed the gaming chair industry.”

Secretlab Titan Evo - K/DA Firestarter Edition

The K/DA design features the Firestarter era's purple flames alongside the Secretlab and K/DA logos. The front of the chair shows each member’s symbols, with silver decals along the edges. The Firestarter edition is available in both Regular ($644) and XL ($714) sizing.

The Magnus Pro is also our top pick for gaming-dedicated desks . In the words of IGN’s reviewer , Mark Knapp, the latest model “combines the metal desktop and versatile cable organization of the original desk with powerful motorized legs to let gamers dial in their fit whether they’re sitting cozy in a chair or standing up, alert and ready to game.”

Secretlab Magnus Pro - K/DA Firestarter Edition

Like the chair, the K/DA edition is covered in smokey flames and the Firestarter insignia. The desk itself starts at $978 directly through Secretlab , which also offers matching hot pink cable management systems at an additional cost.

The launch is accompanied by a new illustration showing the K/DA members in their Firestarter looks working on new music with the Secretlab battlestations:

Rumors began circulating of K/DA’s return when the virtual girl group reactivated their social accounts after six years of silence. The rumors were proven true when a new single titled “Firestarter” dropped in mid-October with a music video animated by long-time Riot Games collaborator Fortiche.

A full EP with the same title was dropped on music streaming services last night. K/DA will also be returning to the stage as the opener for this year's League of Legends World Championship , generally known as Worlds.

articles.title: How the Chicago White Sox Bullpen Shapes up for 2027
articles.summary: ‎The major focus this offseason will be what the Chicago White Sox pitching staff will look like next season. Coming off a high-stakes 2026 postseason campai...
articles.body:
‎The major focus this offseason will be what the Chicago White Sox pitching staff will look like next season. Coming off a high-stakes 2026 postseason campaign, the bullpen was really tested, having been the strength of the team during the regular season. But there will likely be some changes in the bullpen as we head into 2027 (if we have a normal season next year as the Major League Baseball lockout looms). Some changes will be enforced to ensure some of the young arms become starters or head back to the minors for better development.

‎Also, some pitchers have shown they aren't part of the Sox relief corps going forward. Erick Fedde , Trevor Richards and Sean Newcomb are amongst the free agents expected not to be back next season. However, there's a high probability that the White Sox might bring back 33-year-old Newcomb with a short-term deal, considering his consistent performance out of the pen in 2026. But should they allow Newcomb to walk away, it will still be an understandable move by the organization.

The White Sox Bullpen's High Leverage Arms

The White Sox boast of the two most electric, powerful arms in the American League. Grant Taylor and Jordan Hicks are the two most consistent relievers in the Sox bullpen and were pivotal throughout the season. Taylor posted a 2.25 ERA, made 10 saves, and pitched in 84 innings, while striking out 106 batters. The 29-year-old could transition into a starter in 2027, as he carries a devastating, high-spin fastball and sharp breaking balls. However, the central question for next season will be finding consistency as his workload increases, while reducing his walk rate in high-stress games.

‎Hicks, 29, was one of the few pitchers who stepped up in his production in 2026, ultimately earning Will Venable's trust. He recorded a 4.19 ERA in 61 1/3 innings and earned 56 strikeouts. If he can get better control on the mound, he could be a step-up closer. When he's at his best, he's very hard to hit, and when he's off, he walks too many hitters before finding his rhythm. With his fastball pitching strength, if he can keep it in the zone, he can be a key part of the bullpen heading into a walk year.

While the White Sox rely heavily on closers, they also command a strong middle-inning pitching staff that helps dictate the game. One of them is Bryan Hudson , who is under the team's control for next season, which makes him a good innings eater. He pitched in just 67 1/3 innings in 2026, posting a solid 3.74 ERA overall and 59 strikeouts. He's just under 1 WAR, and he's considered a semi-reliable middle guy who isn't on the high-leverage list but is more valuable than just a mop-up pitcher.

‎Tyler Davis didn't get too many opportunities on the mound in 2026, but did his best each time he was called upon. In 32 1/3 innings, he recorded a 3.66 ERA and 37 strikeouts. Davis was part of the roster for the postseason, but pitched just three innings in seven games.

The other player is Huascar Brazobán , who was acquired by the Sox at the trade deadline. He struggled early after arriving in Chicago despite having a good 2026 with the Mets before the trade. Then he joined the injured list for about a month; then he came back and was decent. Brazoban posted a decent 2.96 ERA in 67.0 innings. He didn't make the White Sox's American League Division Series roster. But he's under the team's control through 2029 and could become a key member of the pen by earning Venable's trust.

‎Newcomb is meant to be on this list, but he's not guaranteed another contract offer. Nonetheless, the White Sox will be looking to move on from veteran free agents as they will demand a higher ceiling next season, while making room for younger prospects.

The White Sox will have one of the most fascinating dynamics in 2027 as they will have a strong bullpen but also a sheer volume of young starting pitching talent that is willing to become high-level relief. Hagen Smith , Noah Schultz , David Sandlin , Shane Smith , and Jonathan Cannon are all guys who seem to be likely starters, but any of them could get some time in the bullpen as the season progresses.

‎Mike Vasil and Jordan Leasure will likely be back from injuries, and Sean Burke can be counted on at any time. However, there will be a pitch-count restriction for young arms like Smith and Sandlin, while giving them the right exposure to becoming a top starter. Meanwhile, the White Sox's starting rotation is the biggest question mark, as they need stronger arms so that the young pitchers wouldn't be overtaxed . And the bullpen isn't 100 percent set, and there's still work to be done. But that is less than what needs to be done in the starting rotation. There's hope that the 2027 bullpen will be more solid than the 2026 unit.

articles.title: Yankees linked to offseason trade for Brewers' 18-HR All-Star
articles.summary: The Yankees could be looking for a new catcher.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees may be very busy this offseason.

After falling short in the postseason, general manager Brian Cashman will be looking at potential roster upgrades.

One position of need is at catcher. Austin Wells is a strong defender behind the plate but leaves much to be desired hitting-wise.

New York should be looking for a right-handed platoon partner for Wells in free agency, or they could make a big splash via trade.

Bleacher Report's Zach Buckley believes the Milwaukee Brewers could look to trade William Contreras this offseason, despite the club's run to the World Series.

"Trading Contreras wouldn't help the Brewers now (or maybe any time soon), but it might be what's best for the franchise's future.

"If they aren't prepared to pay what it'll cost to keep him next offseason, then moving him during this one could be the best option on the board," Buckley wrote.

Buckley predicts the Yankees will acquire Contreras, who is one year away from free agency, from the Brewers this winter.

Contreras, a three-time All-Star, is one of the best hitting catchers in baseball. He hit .270/.341/.417 with 18 home runs and a .758 OPS in 147 regular season games.

That offensive production would be a huge upgrade over Wells, who hit .186/.292/.332 with 14 homers and a .624 OPS.

The Yankees would probably have to send Milwaukee one Major League-ready pitcher and a few prospects to secure the trade for Contreras, but it might be worth it to help balance their lineup.

The lineup also covers a wide range of audiences. Music fans get Lil Uzi Vert and A$AP Rocky, anime fans get Luffy, and the vocaloid community gets Miku and Teto. articles.title: How Astros can make trade for Marlins' Cy Young 'without issue'
articles.summary: The Astros could use another frontline starter.
articles.body:
The Houston Astros could use another frontline starting pitcher.

Hunter Brown is the AL West club's ace, but the Astros lack solid rotational depth after Peter Lamber's breakout season.

Even without a new general manager, the Astros should be busy this offseason. They need at least one outfielder and one starter, if not multiple.

FanSided's Jake Elman wrote that the Astros could target Miami Marlins ace Sandy Alcantara. However, the Marlins may prefer to keep Alcantara as they look to compete for a postseason berth in 2027.

"We're honestly not sure whether the Marlins would trade Alcantara, who has a $21 million club option with a $1 million trade assignment bonus. He had an impressive bounce-back season in 2026 with a 3.87 ERA, his lowest since his 2022 NL Cy Young campaign, and he looked more confident as the season progressed," Elman wrote.

Alcantara isn't racking up strikeouts like he used to, punching out just 17.1% of the batters he faced in 2026.

Still, he was a workhorse, finishing the season with a Major League high of 214 innings.

"Alcantara just turned 31, and he'd slot in behind Hunter Brown as the Astros' No. 2 pitcher. We should also note he doesn't have a no-trade clause, so the penny-pinching Marlins could part ways with him without issue," Elman added.

The Astros don't have to jump through hoops if they'd like to acquire Alcantara to be their No. 2 starter. As detailed, he does not have a no-trade clause in his contract.

Houston's front office should definitley target rotation upgrades this winter, and Alcantara is an intriguing option who will earn a reasonable $21 million next season.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts missiles and drones as fighting with Houthis rages
articles.summary: Saudi-led coalition says intercepted drone, missile launched towards Riyadh and 10 missiles targeting southern region.
articles.body:
Saudi Arabia has intercepted drones and missiles over its capital, Riyadh, and southern areas, the Saudi-led coalition has said, as fighting with Yemen’s Houthis continues.

Coalition spokesman Major-General Turki al-Maliki said on Sunday its forces intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launched towards the capital city that morning, as well as a drone in the Riyadh region, and a cruise missile aimed at the southwestern city of Khamis Mushait, with explosions ringing out in the Saudi capital.

It later reported the interception of 10 ballistic missiles fired towards southern ‌Saudi Arabia.

The attacks come as operations resumed at two terminals at Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid international airport after deadly attacks earlier this month by the Houthis, an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God).

Operations at the airport were halted on October 10 after 13 people were killed and more than 300 others were wounded in a Houthi attack .

Late on Saturday, Riyadh airport said in a statement that international flights would resume from Terminal 2 on Sunday, while Terminal 1 would be designated for domestic flights.

Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree warned that the airport was still “unsafe” and a “military target” for the Iran-backed group.

“The Yemeni Armed Forces warn all international, regional and local airlines – as well as staff and travellers – against using King Khalid airport in Riyadh, as it is unsafe and serves as a military target for our forces,” he said. “The Saudi regime shall bear the consequences of any operations at the airport.”

The Iran-aligned Houthis on Saturday said they targeted three Saudi airports, including one in Riyadh, energy installations, a pipeline and an airbase.

The Saudi civil defence agency said it also responded to falling debris in the Mecca and Medina regions on Saturday after intercepting two Houthi missiles.

The Houthis denied targeting Mecca and Medina, two of the holiest cities in Islam, calling the Saudi claim a “huge lie”.

In Yemen on Sunday, the Houthis advanced on Jabal Sabr, the strategic mountain overlooking the city of Taiz, which has become the focus of the fighting between the Houthis and Yemen’s government forces.

Houthi fighters have besieged the city and cut off the main road to Aden, which serves as the interim capital of Yemen’s internationally recognised government.

The United Nations has warned that “time is running out” to deliver aid to the 800,000 people trapped in the city.

Yemen’s government forces, meanwhile, said they conducted more than 700 operations against Houthi targets on Saturday, claiming to have killed more than 300 fighters.

Fighting between government forces and Houthi fighters has intensified across multiple fronts in Yemen in recent weeks, causing a spiralling humanitarian crisis .

The war in Yemen escalated sharply when the Houthis seized strategic territory from forces loyal to the country’s internationally recognised government along the Red Sea coast last month.

The Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, which is aligned with Yemen’s government forces, have dealt a huge blow to the kingdom, the world’s biggest exporter of crude oil, disrupting its businesses, airlines and normal life, and damaging its international image.
